title: Alternative formula for input lag lower bound
body:
The current formula for input lag lower bound is giving innacurate results in some scenarios.

Lets assume an input lag model with the following steps:

1.4 - present() (frame i-2)
2.1 - sleep() (frame i-1)
2.2 - input() (frame i-1)
2.3 - cpu() (frame i-1)
2.4 - present() (frame i-1)
3.1 - sleep() (frame i)
3.2 - input() (frame i)
3.3 - cpu() (frame i)
3.4 - present() (frame i)
3.5 - display() (frame i)

sleep() is used by frame rate limiters to control frame speed.
input() is the user mouse/keyboard input.
cpu() is the frame being rendered by the game engine.
present() and display() are steps monitored by PresentMon.

The lower bound should be the time between steps 3.2 (frame i input) and 3.5 (frame i display).
The upper bound should be the time between steps 2.2 (frame i-1 input) and 3.5 (frame i display).

PresentMon gives us the following numbers:
MsBetweenPresents[i] - time between steps 2.4 and 3.4
MsUntilDisplayed[i] - time between steps 3.4 and 3.5
MsBetweenPresents[i-1] - time between steps 1.4 and 2.4
MsInPresentAPI[i-1] - time between steps 2.4 and 3.1
MsInPresentAPI[i-2] - time between steps 1.4 and 2.1

Since sleep(), input() and cpu() steps are not monitored by PresentMon, we have to guess values in order to estimate lower and upper bounds for input lag.
If we assume sleep() time is high and cpu() time is low we get a low input lag estimation as result, which can be used for a lower bound estimation. 
If we assume sleep() time is low and cpu() time is high we get a high input lag estimation as result, which can be used for an upper bound estimation. 

If we assume sleep() = MsBetweenPresents (time between steps 2.4 and 3.4) and assume cpu() = 0, the lower bound should be:
steps 3.2 to 3.4 = 0 ms.
steps 3.4 to 3.5 = MsUntilDisplayed

So, the formula for the input lag lower bound should be equal to MsUntilDisplayed alone, without MsBetweenPresents and MsInPresentAPI.
For the upper bound, we can assume sleep() = 0 and cpu() = MsBetweenPresents. Which leads to the same upper bound formula already in use in CapFrameX version 1.6.5.

**`Lower bound = MsUntilDisplayed[i]`**
`Upper bound = MsBetweenPresents[i] + MsUntilDisplayed[i] + MsBetweenPresents[i-1] - MsInPresentAPI[i-2]`

The scenario above for the lower bound should happen when CapFrameX is used to measure simple games with VSync ON and using a frame rate limiter which sleeps outside the present() call (i.e. RTSS). In this scenario, cpu() is low, sleep() is high and MsInPresentAPI[i-1] is low. The real input lag will be lower than the estimated lower bound with the current formula (version 1.6.5), but should be higher than the new proposed formula.

title: Log render latency contributions (feature request)
body:
Well outside my lane here. Maybe I'm asking for something that's not feasible.

It would be extremely handy if CapframeX could log what took how long in each frame. For example in frame 1 the CPU took 1.5ms to prepare the frame, 0.1ms to submit the frame, then the GPU took 4ms to render the frame etc for a total frame time of 4.6ms. Basically this (https://imgur.com/nCdO4qw) but logged per frame. The more substeps that could be included the better.

This would _massively_ simplify doing configuration and bottleneck testing, as well as troubleshooting games that are inconsistently performant (for eg when a stutter occurs was it a GPU choke or a CPU choke or was the CPU actually starved by RAM etc). title: Project TaigaCat Plugin Support for CFX
body:
Hi, thought I'd create this thread to discuss how I should go about implementing Project TaigaCat's real time capture card analysis features into CapFrameX.  This is mostly useful for game console benchmarking (ala Digital Foundry).

I guess I'll start with my proposal on how it'll be implemented, please let me know any suggestions/tweaks you'd like to see and I'd be happy to investigate supporting/changing them

- Project TaigaCat for CapFrameX will be implemented as a separate plugin .dll
  - This .dll will of course be written in C#, open source under the MIT License in line with the rest of the program
  - I feel that keeping this functionality separate would be a better idea than natively adding it to the main application as the process for capture card based benchmarking differs from typical "native" PC benchmarking
  - This also allows the two to be worked on and updated (mostly) independently of each other
- CFX will call the plugin's init method, and the plugin will start-up and report back a list of all webcams connected to the PC (capture cards present themselves as virtual webcams)
- The user can select the appropriate capture device from CFX, which then will let the plugin know which device the user has selected
- The plugin then tells CFX how the capture card is configured (resolution, refresh rate, bit depth) so CFX has the info it needs to setup any recordings/graphs/whatever on the application side
  - If CFX needs any additional info than this just let me know
- CFX can request several things from the plugin
  - The current frame from the capture card
  - The current configuration of the plugin (capture card name, resolution, refresh rate, bit depth, and frame comparison confidence level)
  - Ask the plugin if a new frame has been rendered (aka attempt to determine if the source is dropping frames)
  - Ask the plugin what the current frametime/framerate is based on capture card analysis
  - Ask the plugin for the average, standard deviation and coefficient of variation for pixel differences of the last analysis
  - Change the target capture device and analysis confidence level
- Frame analysis currently is done by calculating a confidence level that two frames are the same
  - First the current/previous frames are converted to a 3D matrix with each table entry holding the RGB color channels of the appropriate pixel
  - The matrices are subtracted, and then we determine the distance in the RGB color space of each pixel from the previous frame's pixel
  - The average, standard deviation and coefficient of variation are determined
  - The frame's confidence level is simply 1.0 - the coefficient of variation
  - If the frame's confidence level exceeds the confidence level set by the user (in other words, we believe the frames are similar enough), then it's marked as a dropped frame

Apologies in advance for the wall of text (writing isn't my strong suit), and please let me know what suggestions/tweaks you'd like to see.  I'll try to have an alpha ASAP (though bear with me as I have a somewhat busy schedule and it's been a LONG time since I dealt with webcam access in .NET)

Cheers!

title: Feature request: Display highest-load CPU thread/core
body:
It's common to have a "CPU utilization" value calculated as an average utilization across all logical CPU threads (as displayed in Windows Task Manager), but this is of limited use to the observer unless they are using applications which scale across many threads. Most applications DON'T scale across many threads, so you can end up with an uncomfortable situation where a 16 thread CPU is delivering maximum possible performance to an application yet the "CPU utilization" only says "6%". Compounding this poor communication is how Windows can rapidly move software threads around to different hardware threads, precluding the observer from pinning one logical thread for monitoring, confusing monitoring application algorithms, and obfuscating the true single-thread CPU load and application usage. As new CPUs are delivered with more cores and threads, this problem is amplified, and common "CPU utilization" monitoring becomes useless, with many tasks not being visible on utilization graphs despite clocking up a CPU to maximum boost and fully using one thread or core.

I propose a novel "max CPU single-thread utilization" (MCSTU) metric and accompanying "max CPU single-thread utilization application" metric for monitoring applications, so people can see when their CPU is being used, and by what application. These are complimentary to the "average" CPU and GPU utilization values commonly shown in monitoring applications ever since the days of 1-core CPUs where the average and the max was the same thing. Note the same phenomenon of average equaling max in many-core GPUs where all applications are maximally threaded.

Thank you for reading!

title: Develop/feature/jenkins fix
Show frametimes for CPU/GPU separately.
body:
fpsVR has a very handy feature where it displays frametimes separately for the CPU and GPU rather than showing the overall frametime. I find this information useful for better determining what is causing FPS issues, because at the very least I know what hardware the lengthy processing time or spikes in processing time are happening on even though I may not know the actual cause, which gives me a better idea of how to debug things when I run into issues.

Right now the only tool I know that allows you to look at latencies in flatscreen games that are broken down into more than just an overall frametime is SpecialK (see third screenshot), however it isn't exactly safe to use in multiplayer games (some people have reported getting banned from games when using it).

It would be awesome if CapFrameX could show frametimes for CPU and GPU separately like fpsVR does. SpecialK's output is nice for advanced analysis, but I don't know if most people would need that much data, unless of course they're doing latency analysis in reviews like Gamers Nexus does.

I am writing here in the hope of finding a solution to my problem. I have been using MSI Afterburner for many years, and it has always worked well. Could you please assist me in troubleshooting this problem? I am using Windows 11, updated with the latest updates, and my video card is an RTX 3090.

title: PresentMode in overlay
body:
Hi,
Is it possible to add PresentMode (from PresentMon) somehow in the overlay?
Or even more - to be integrated in the json captures and in the analysis.

Use case is the following. I use CX to do some benchmarks and optimizations and I am testing different scenarios - fullscreen/windowed/FSO/MPO/vsync/gsync... that may have impact on the present mode chosen by the app/dwm. And besides the resulting frame times I would like to know what was the present mode. Currently I need to manually check in presentmon csv in order to see it. (Or other way for me is to just run separate instance of presentmon to capture few seconds just to see the mode in the file).
It would be best if I can see it in the overlay before i run the benchmark.

I know it is possible to use RTSS additional overlay plugin to add prsentmon as datasource and display the mode in the overlay, but that is something that I don't want to do, because it may have the "observer effect" (changing the present mode, and probably also performance because of the overlay) .
CX overlay as far as I understand is actually not "overlay" but inprint via RTSS so it would not have the "observer effect", so that is the reason for my request.

I saw some past requests/discussions about it, I just hoped few years later this feature can can get into CX :)

Regards,
Georgi

title: Minimize CX window to the system tray function stopped working after installing CX v.1.7.2
body:
After installing the latest CapFrameX 1.7.2 release build, minimizing the program window to the Windows system tray is not possible anymore.

Once the program window is opened/shown, only minimizing into the taskbar is allowed using the Minimize window button. So, now, the CapFrameX program (processes) cannot run in the background when minimized once the window has been opened or shown.

However, the minimize to the system tray function still works the first time you launch CX (before opening/showing the program window for the first time after launch) on 1.7.2 when the "Start minimized" APP setting is enabled.

Could you restore the minimizing to the system tray behavior or (re)implement the function once the application window is opened or shown?

Best regards.

title: Feature Request: GPU Busy Deviation considering target frame rate
body:
I'm not sure if this is possible. I use GPU Busy deviation to understand if the CPU is holding back my GPU. But GPU busy deviation does not account for FPS being at frame cap (e.g. max refresh rate of display).

1st example: If frame rate cap (e.g. max refresh rate of display) is reached (i.e. CPU not holding back GPU), GPU Busy Deviation value can still be high. For me this isn't a deviation because the CPU is delivering the necessary frame time and the GPU is busy enough to reach my target frame rate.

2nd example: If frame rate cap (e.g. max refresh rate of display) cannot be reached (i.e. CPU is holding back GPU utilization), closing the gap indicated by the GPU Busy deviation value would bring the frame rate above the target frame rate.

Would it make sense to add a target frame rate value that GPU busy deviation can account for?

title: system wide PawnIO issues/conflicts
body:
Tested with release_1.7.7_#36 as well as 09/12 installer.

Whenever you exit CapFrameX it will attempt to stop system wide PawnIO driver, which can be observed with e.g.
```
C:\Utils\CapFrameX>sc query PawnIO

SERVICE_NAME: PawnIO
        TYPE               : 1  KERNEL_DRIVER
        STATE              : 3  STOP_PENDING
                                (STOPPABLE, NOT_PAUSABLE, IGNORES_SHUTDOWN)
        WIN32_EXIT_CODE    : 0  (0x0)
        SERVICE_EXIT_CODE  : 0  (0x0)
        CHECKPOINT         : 0x0
        WAIT_HINT          : 0x0
```

- stop is pending until I close or kill other software using this driver (e.g. FanControl in my case) - after which the driver will transition to stopped state. After that I have to start it manually.
- while the stop is pending - if I start CapFrameX it will be unable to provide some readings (e.g. cpu mhz metrics)

Overall it seems that CapFrameX still uses system wide PawnIO driver if it exists in the system. Some kind of detection would probably be needed as well as making sure it doesn't try to stop such system-wide driver on exit.

title: Overlay 1% Low should use MsBetweenDisplayChange instead of MsBetweenPresents
body:
I’m not 100% sure what metric the Overlay is currently using for 1% Low, but based on the numbers I see when MFG (Multiframe Generation) is enabled, it looks like it might be relying on:

MsBetweenPresents Per Frame → the time between the current Present call and the previous one (in ms).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15cc9335-c626-48ac-a735-a5fac254f352)

NVIDIA App report 1% Low is about 75 fps in same frame.
What I’d like to suggest is switching to:

MsBetweenDisplayChange Per Frame → the time between when the previous frame was actually shown on the display and when the current frame was shown (in ms).

Why this matters:

MsBetweenPresents only reflects the timing of Present calls in the rendering pipeline.

MsBetweenDisplayChange reflects the actual change on screen, which is closer to what the user really experiences.

With MFG enabled, the difference becomes important: Present intervals can look artificially low, while display change intervals give a more accurate picture of frame pacing.

Expected behavior:

Overlay should report 1% Low based on MsBetweenDisplayChange.

This would make the metric more reliable and representative of real-world performance, especially when MFG is active.

title: Feature Request: "Top CPU Processes" Snapshot during frametime spikes
body:
When a random FPS drop or stutter occurs, it is currently impossible to identify which background process (e.g., Windows Update, Anti-Virus, or a background utility) caused the CPU spike. Since these spikes are often gone in a split second, "Alt-Tabbing" to Task Manager doesn't work.

I suggest adding a "Top CPU Processes" snapshot feature. To avoid the high overhead of logging every single process constantly, the app could capture a "snapshot" of the top 3–5 CPU-consuming .exe files only when a frametime spike is detected (or as a lightweight log during the capture).
This would allow users to easily cross-compare a spike in the frametime graph with a specific background program name.

Using "Windows Performance Recorder" or "Process Monitor," but these are very complex for average users and high in overhead.

By only capturing the "Top 5" offenders, the performance impact on the benchmark should remain very low while providing massive troubleshooting value.

Fixed an issue where certain cyclic or self-referential object graphs could trigger uncontrolled recursion during mapping, potentially resulting in stack exhaustion and denial of service.

Applications that process untrusted or attacker-controlled object graphs through affected mapping paths may be impacted.

Users should upgrade to this release.

Security advisory: GHSA-rvv3-g6hj-g44x

Thanks to @​bluefossa for responsibly disclosing this issue.

This release supersedes the 15.0.0 release, reverting behavior and overloads so that the `AddAutoMapper` overloads separate the "scanning for maps" from the "scanning for dependencies". Unfortunately it's not really possible to combine these two together.

Because of this, the 15.0.0 will be delisted because of the breaking changes there.

## 15.0.0

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/compare/v14.0.0...v15.0.0

* Added support for .NET Standard 2.0
* Requiring license key
* Moving from MIT license to dual commercial/OSS license

To set your license key:

```csharp
services.AddAutoMapper(cfg => {
    cfg.LicenseKey = "<License key here>";
});
```

This also introduced a breaking change with `MapperConfiguration` requiring an `ILoggerFactory` for logging purposes:

```csharp
public MapperConfiguration(MapperConfigurationExpression configurationExpression, ILoggerFactory loggerFactory)
```

Registering AutoMapper with `services.AddAutoMapper` will automatically supply this parameter. Otherwise you'll need to supply the logger factory.

You can obtain your license key at [AutoMapper.io](https://automapper.io)

title: Bump AutoMapper and Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions
body:
Updated [AutoMapper](https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper) from 9.0.0 to 15.1.1.

<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>

_Sourced from [AutoMapper's releases](https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/releases)._

## 15.1.1

## What's Changed
* docs: Document duplicate license message behavior and fixes by @​Copilot in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4617

## Security

Fixed an issue where certain cyclic or self-referential object graphs could trigger uncontrolled recursion during mapping, potentially resulting in stack exhaustion and denial of service.

Applications that process untrusted or attacker-controlled object graphs through affected mapping paths may be impacted.

Users should upgrade to this release.

Security advisory: GHSA-rvv3-g6hj-g44x

Thanks to @​skdishansachin for responsibly disclosing this issue.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/compare/v16.1.1...v15.1.1

## 15.1.0

## What's Changed
* remove Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub by @​SimonCropp in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4555
* Direct .NET 4.x support by @​jbogard in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4569
* Bumping the JsonWebTokens because of GHSA-8g4q-xg66-9fp4; fixes #​4575 by @​jbogard in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4576
* Provide better exceptions for errors when building the mapping plan by @​jbogard in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4577
* Adding docs for license configuration by @​jbogard in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4581
* Updating refs to fix missing method issue by @​jbogard in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4582

## New Contributors
* @​SimonCropp made their first contribution in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4555

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/compare/v15.0.1...v15.1.0

## 15.0.1

## What's Changed
* Removing public signing; fixes #​4545 by @​jbogard in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4552
* Adding back missing overloads and reverting registering behavior by @​jbogard in https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/pull/4554


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/compare/v15.0.0...v15.0.1

This release supersedes the 15.0.0 release, reverting behavior and overloads so that the `AddAutoMapper` overloads separate the "scanning for maps" from the "scanning for dependencies". Unfortunately it's not really possible to combine these two together.

This also fixes a critical bug in #​4545 that does not work with .NET 4.x applications (as intended).

Because of this, the 15.0.0 will be delisted because of the breaking changes there.

## 15.0.0

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper/compare/v14.0.0...v15.0.0

* Added support for .NET Standard 2.0
* Requiring license key
* Moving from MIT license to dual commercial/OSS license

To set your license key:

```csharp
services.AddAutoMapper(cfg => {
    cfg.LicenseKey = "<License key here>";
});
```

This also introduced a breaking change with `MapperConfiguration` requiring an `ILoggerFactory` for logging purposes:

```csharp
public MapperConfiguration(MapperConfigurationExpression configurationExpression, ILoggerFactory loggerFactory)
```

Registering AutoMapper with `services.AddAutoMapper` will automatically supply this parameter. Otherwise you'll need to supply the logger factory.

You can obtain your license key at [AutoMapper.io](https://automapper.io)

## 14.0.0

## What's Changed
* Reverted the nullable annotations by @​lbargaoanu in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4390
* Fix polymorphic mapping when some derived types have explicit mappings and others do not by @​kev-andrews in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4402
* The default naming conventions for a profile should come from the glo… by @​lbargaoanu in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4428
* Fix Issue #​4502 - Confusing exception when trying to map types with … by @​Biotronic in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4503
* Target .net 8 and seal more classes by @​lbargaoanu in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4474
* Target .Net 9 in tests by @​lbargaoanu in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4507
* Changed lock-threads parameters by @​lbargaoanu in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4516
* Don't throw and catch on validation by @​lbargaoanu in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4526

## New Contributors
* @​kev-andrews made their first contribution in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4402
* @​Biotronic made their first contribution in https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/pull/4503

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/compare/v13.0.1...v14.0.0

## 13.0.1

title: Most VRAM overlay options not appearing since beta 1.7.6
body: I've noticed in updates since beta 1.7.6 that certain VRAM metrics have been missing. I would usually track _**'GPU Memory Dedicated/Used'**_ for overall usage and _**'GPU Memory Dedicated Game'**_ for the per process usage. Which would look like this: With releases 1.7.7 and 1.7.8 (from what I've checked) they do not have the _**'GPU Memory Dedicated Game'**_ metric anymore, but some other option are still available: Now on the more recent releases, even more VRAM metrics have vanished. This example is on an RX 9070 XT and other AMD cards have the same problem– you can basically only track the _**'GPU Memory Dedicated'**_ and do not have the _**'Used'**_ version: I can't find the options anywhere in the list, correct me if I'm wrong though. This isn't exactly the same on Nvidia GPUs– on v1.8.4 you can get _**'GPU Memory Dedicated'**_ and _**'GPU Memory Used'**_, but still no _**'GPU Memory Dedicated Game'**_ on either. I have personally been sticking to the older beta 1.7.6 version just so I can maintain this metric but now that version is running into compatibility problems with new HW like Pantherlake not detecting sensors and the _**'GPU Memory Dedicated Game'**_ shows up as a crazy high number in the new Crimson Desert release (attached an image of that). I've been super confused why the metrics have been disappearing and if it is on my end, then please let me know. Thanks for any help you can give!

title: Present Timing not working on Linux
body:
Currently (https://github.com/CXWorld/CapFrameX/commit/3ba66ff508303ed669c37a37e1b6391939391e2a) there seems to be an issue with the **Present Timing** measurements on Linux. 

Despite the obvious hard requirement of VK_EXT_present_timing being satisfied, CapFrameX does not enable **Present Timing** based measurements for any of the workloads tested.

Native Vulkan apps, such as "vkcube" or the samples from ([SaschaWillems/Vulkan](https://github.com/SaschaWillems/Vulkan)) only have **Layer Timing** available. 

Meanwhile Proton, which itself currently does not support "VK_EXT_present_timing" shows **Present Timing** being enabled after applying this patch https://github.com/HansKristian-Work/vkd3d-proton/commit/f2f6da6b9fcb3c976d774a10b24ef1d25987e0b8. However, even despite CapframeX now stating **Present Timing** is being used, the MsActualPresent column in the logs is all zero with MsBetweenPresents still being the only available value.

Arch Linux 6.19.9-arch1-1 using Wayland
mesa 26.1.0 (Dev g718afd78)
vulkan-headers 1.4.341.0-1
vulkan-icd-loader 1.4.341.0-1
vulkan-tools 1.4.341.0-2

title: Misleading FrameView SDK installer referenced in CLAUDE.md
body:
## Description

The build documentation in ``CLAUDE.md`` lists the FrameView SDK as a prerequisite and states:

> FrameView SDK (installer at ``installers/FVSDKSetup.exe``)

However, the ``installers/`` directory and ``FVSDKSetup.exe`` file do not exist in the repository.

## Suggested Resolution

One solution I can think of is to update ``CLAUDE.md`` to include information on how to obtain the FrameView SDK installer (download link, version, etc.). Additionally, adding ``installers/`` or ``installers/FVSDKSetup.exe`` to ``.gitignore`` would clarify that this file is meant to be downloaded separately and is not tracked in the repository.

This would make the ``CLAUDE.md`` build instructions more widely applicable for new AI agents on new machines.

title: Sensor "GPU Power (%)" reacts to RGB Lighting and Fan Speed
body:
**My System:**
- OS: Windows 11
- GPU: GIGABYTE GeForce RTX 5080 GAMING OC 16G (GV-N5080GAMING OC-16GD)
- Motherboard: ASUS ROG STRIX B650E-F GAMING WIFI

**What I tested:**
I enabled `GPU Power (W)`, `GPU Power (%)`, and `GPU Board Power (%)` in the overlay. Then, I opened the RivaTuner Overlay Editor to inspect the provided sensor values while the GPU was under very low load (RTSS app → blue Setup button → Plugins tab → double-click `OverlayEditor.dll`).

Next, I opened the Gigabyte Control Center to configure fan speed and RGB lighting. First, I reduced power usage to a minimum by disabling the lighting and setting the fan speed to 0 RPM (Auto Fan Control with fan stop below 50 °C). As expected, “Power” and “Board Power” were almost equal, at around 5–6%.

Then, I enabled maximum fan speed (3000 RPM), and `GPU Power (W)` increased from roughly 21.5 W to 28.5 W. Additionally, both percentage values increased to 7–8%.

Measuring the impact of RGB lighting was more difficult, since its effect on power usage was rather small. However, I think (though I’m not entirely sure) that both percentage values reacted equally to the white lighting as well.

---

Maybe this is the intended and expected behavior, but when I see a distinction between “GPU Power” and “GPU Board Power,” I would expect only “GPU Power” to include fan and lighting power consumption.

I was already skeptical about the distinction between “Board Power” and “Power” before I started testing. As far as I know (which is actually not that much, so I could also just stfu), NVIDIA doesn’t provide clear information about the exact meaning of their sensors. So maybe this is simply a case of incorrect labeling.

title: FPS metrics become NaN after running for a while, while Frametime still updates
body: ## Description After running CapFrameX for a while, several live OSD metrics stop updating correctly and become `NaN`, while the frametime value/graph and hardware sensor values continue to update normally. The issue does not happen immediately after starting CapFrameX. At first, the OSD metrics display correctly. After some runtime, the following values become invalid: - `Real-time average FPS`: `NaN FPS` - `Real-time 1% Low FPS`: `NaN FPS` - `GPU Active Time Average / GPUBusy`: `NaN ms` - `GPU Active Time Deviation`: `NaN %` - Runtime line such as `D3D12`: `0 FPS` At the same time, these values still work: - `Frametime` continues updating normally - The frametime graph continues moving - GPU/CPU/RAM sensor values continue updating normally Restarting CapFrameX immediately restores the OSD metrics, but the issue comes back after running for a while. ## Environment - CapFrameX version: `1.8.5` - Mode: Portable mode - PresentMon: `PresentMon-2.4.1-x64` - RTSS: `7.3.7` - OS: Windows 11 25H2, Build: 26200.8457 - GPU: `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU` - CPU: `AMD Ryzen AI 7 H 350 w/ Radeon 860M` - Game/API: `Onimusha: Way of the Sword (Demo)` or any `D3D12` game - .NET Desktop Runtime: `9.0.16 x64` ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start CapFrameX `1.8.5` in portable mode. 2. Start a D3D12 game. 3. Enable OSD entries such as: - `Frametime` - `Real-time average FPS` - `Real-time 1% Low FPS` - `GPU Active Time / GPUBusy` - GPU/CPU/RAM sensors 4. Let the game and OSD run for some time. 5. Observe that online FPS/statistical metrics eventually become `NaN`, while `Frametime` and hardware sensors continue updating. ## Expected Behavior Live online metrics should continue updating as long as frametime data is still available. For example, if `Frametime` is around `9.5 ms`, `Real-time average FPS` should be around `105 FPS`. ## Actual Behavior After some runtime: ```text Average FPS: NaN 1% Low: NaN GPUBusy: NaN ms / NaN % D3D12: 0 FPS Frametime: still valid, e.g. 9.5 ms ``` ## Recovery Tests The following actions do **not** recover the invalid metrics: - `Alt + M` / Reset metrics hotkey - `Alt + O` / Toggle overlay off and on The following action **does** recover the metrics: - Restarting CapFrameX ## Process Check When the issue is happening, only one CapFrameX and one PresentMon process are running: ```text CapFrameX PresentMon-2.4.1-x64 RTSS RTSSHooksLoader64 ``` No duplicate CapFrameX or duplicate PresentMon processes were observed. ## Diagnostics CapFrameX MCP/status reports capture state as stopped and not locked: ```json { "isCapturing": false, "isLocked": false, "delayCountdownRunning": false, "osdAutoDisabled": false, "state": "Stopped" } ``` Recent CapFrameX diagnostics did not report a new PresentMon error when the OSD metrics became `NaN`. ## Notes This does not look like a total PresentMon failure, because the live frametime value/graph continues to update normally. It looks more like the online metrics/statistics stream or live FPS aggregation gets stuck or invalidated while the raw frametime OSD path remains alive. ## Attachments - OSD screenshot showing `GPUBusy: NaN` , `1% Low: NaN`, `D3D12: 0 FPS` while `Frametime` still updates - `CapFrameX.log` from the portable logs folder: [CapFrameX.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28545476/CapFrameX.log)

title: Improve capture analysis performance and responsiveness
body:
## Summary

This change improves the responsiveness of record discovery, analysis, comparison, aggregation, and graph rendering while tightening the correctness of frametime-derived metrics and plotted data.

The branch starts at the exact `v1.8.6` commit (`383bc029`) and introduces no runtime or package dependencies.

## What changed

### Faster record discovery and loading

- Scan JSON metadata without deserializing the full frame and sensor payload merely to populate the record list.
- Parse only required CSV columns with a quote-aware, allocation-conscious reader.
- Reuse unchanged sessions through a bounded weak-reference/LRU cache; concurrent callers share one load operation.
- Cache record metadata in memory and in a bounded, versioned binary index built entirely with BCL APIs.
- Validate cached entries by normalized path, file length, and last-write time; invalidate on writes and recover safely from corrupt or stale indexes.
- Preserve process-list naming behavior across both memory and persistent metadata caches.

### More efficient and accurate statistics

- Batch FPS and frametime metric calculation so percentile inputs are sorted once instead of once per metric.
- Reuse exact sorted sequences while still detecting in-place sample mutation.
- Replace dense frametime-distribution work with a sparse, time-weighted accumulation algorithm.
- Correct deci-percentile removal at exact sample boundaries and retain constant sequences.
- Filter invalid timing samples consistently and preserve the original timestamps after outlier removal.
- Keep average FPS present-based while selecting display-change timing for low metrics only when every compared run supports it.
- Return the unchanged source for unsupported outlier modes instead of propagating `null`.

### More responsive and faithful visualization

- Perform record loading and expensive analysis work outside the WPF UI thread.
- Serialize selection loads and use cancellation/version guards so stale work cannot overwrite newer selections.
- Separate cancellation families for full analysis and threshold-only refreshes.
- Debounce rapid option changes and redraw immediately when the configured timing source changes.
- Decimate dense OxyPlot line rendering per screen column while preserving endpoints, minima, maxima, gaps, source tracker points, zoom behavior, and exports.
- Correct plot labels/axes, keep distribution plots anchored at zero, and clear plots when the session becomes invalid.
- Align GPU-active clipboard series by timestamp intersection and remove non-finite points instead of relying on matching array indices.
- Enable explicit WPF recycling virtualization for the main record and aggregation grids.

### Safer concurrent UI state

- Make comparison timing-source selection all-or-nothing across records and expose the selected source in the UI.
- Make aggregation add/update operations transactional, with rollback and cleanup on cancellation or failure.
- Observe and log background sensor-report faults.
- Separate online metric buffers to remove a cross-lock race.

### Regression coverage and developer workflow

- Add focused tests for session reuse/invalidation, concurrent loads, persistent-index recovery, process-list renames, incomplete JSON, quoted CSV, distribution math, timing-cache mutation, outlier handling, display-source fallback, timestamp alignment, and plot decimation.
- Add `Build-And-Run.ps1` for a one-command x64 Release restore/build/launch workflow. It discovers a compatible Visual Studio toolchain and may request elevation to install missing v143/MFC/C++/CLI components.

## Positive impact

- Record-list refreshes avoid loading full capture object graphs, reducing both startup I/O and allocation pressure.
- Reopening unchanged captures is effectively a cache lookup rather than a repeat parse.
- Rapid selection and settings changes remain responsive and cannot publish stale calculations.
- Large graphs draw far fewer screen points without hiding short spikes, dips, gaps, or endpoints.
- Frametime distributions no longer scale with `sample count x bin count`, avoiding severe stalls on long captures or isolated large hitches.
- Average, 1%, 0.2%, 0.1%, percentile, integral-low, threshold, and distribution results share validated timing inputs and explicit timing-source rules.

Indicative local synthetic benchmarks during development (hardware/data dependent):

- Sixteen metrics over 1,000,000 samples: about **64 ms batched** versus **279 ms** through repeated per-metric calls (~4.4x faster); an unchanged cached repeat was about **1.4 ms**.
- A 200,000-sample time-weighted distribution containing a 10-second hitch: about **13 ms** versus **46 s** for the previous dense traversal (~3,500x faster for that stress case).

## Compatibility and behavior notes

- No SQLite, database engine, or new NuGet dependency is introduced.
- The persistent metadata index is disposable acceleration data: stale/corrupt entries fall back to source parsing and are rebuilt.
- Correct quote-aware CSV selection can intentionally produce a different hash from the old parser when quoted fields contain commas, because the selected/analyzed rows are now the rows represented by the CSV.
- A final deferred metadata-index update can be lost on forced process termination; capture data remains safe and the index is rebuilt later.

## Validation

- `x64 Release` application build: **passed**, 0 errors.
- `x64 Release` test assembly build: **passed**, 0 errors.
- Full MSTest run: **297 total, 292 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed**.
- The five skips require a live PresentMon-compatible capture target/hardware environment.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

## Run locally

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Build-And-Run.ps1
```

title: Add one-command x64 build and run script
body:
## Summary

This extracts the build/run helper from #398 into a tooling-only PR, following the review request.

`Build-And-Run.ps1` restores dependencies, discovers a compatible Visual Studio toolchain, builds x64 Release, and launches CapFrameX from one command.

## Scope and safety

- Adds one PowerShell script only; no application, project, package, or runtime changes.
- Normal restore/build work is non-elevated.
- Visual Studio component installation requires the explicit `-InstallPrerequisites` switch and UAC confirmation.
- Tracks the CapFrameX process launched by this checkout using a per-checkout temporary state file, validated by PID, process name, and start time.
- Discovers the tracked CapFrameX instance's PresentMon child and requests elevation only when those tracked elevated processes must be stopped before rebuilding.
- Existing path-based cleanup remains restricted to this checkout's output executables.
- Uses single-node, non-reused MSBuild because the legacy native projects otherwise intermittently contend for shared PDB writers (`C1041`/`mspdbsrv`).
- Build-server shutdown is guarded so cleanup cannot mask an earlier error.

## Validation

- PowerShell parser validation: passed.
- NuGet/runtime restore: passed.
- x64 Release build: passed, 0 errors.
- Repeated-run testing identified and fixed elevated CapFrameX/PresentMon file-lock handling.
- Final read-only safety audit: passed; PID/name/start-time validation, per-checkout state isolation, output-path restrictions, and guarded cleanup were rechecked.
- A final interactive double-run through the UAC prompt remains a recommended manual smoke test, but the audited code fails safely if the prompt is declined.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Usage

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Build-And-Run.ps1
```

Only if required Visual Studio components are missing:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Build-And-Run.ps1 -InstallPrerequisites
```

This PR is based directly on `v1.8.6` (`383bc029`).

title: Improve record parsing and in-memory loading
body:
## Summary

This extracts the record parsing/loading work from #398 into a focused change, following the review request.

The goal is to reduce record-list I/O and repeated parsing while keeping cache behavior bounded, disposable, and validated against the source file.

## Changes

- Add a 16-entry weak session cache keyed by normalized path, file length, and last-write time.
- Share one `Lazy<ISession>` between concurrent callers loading the same unchanged capture.
- Invalidate session and metadata entries immediately after successful JSON/CSV application writes.
- Scan JSON metadata without deserializing frame and sensor payloads merely to populate the record list.
- Add a bounded 4,096-entry in-memory metadata cache with source-stamp validation.
- Refresh ProcessList-derived display names instead of freezing them in cached metadata.
- Parse only required CSV fields with quote-aware handling for quoted commas and escaped quotes.
- Use the same quote-aware reader in dominant-swap-chain selection and metric conversion.
- Reuse already-read CSV lines when constructing record metadata.
- Compute the selected-row SHA-1 incrementally while preserving the existing hash contract for ordinary captures.
- Reject incomplete JSON metadata instead of presenting records that cannot be analyzed.

## Deliberately excluded

- No persistent binary metadata index.
- No SQLite or database work.
- No new package/runtime dependency.
- No statistics, WPF, plotting, or build-tooling changes.

The persistent-index portion remains local because CapFrameX 2.0 plans to use SQLite.

## Regression coverage

Ten focused tests cover session reuse, stamp invalidation, concurrent sharing, immediate post-write cache invalidation, hash compatibility, dominant swap-chain behavior, JSON metadata parity/reuse, ProcessList renames, incomplete JSON, and quoted CSV fields.

## Validation

- x64 Release application build: passed, 0 errors.
- x64 Release test build: passed, 0 errors.
- Focused record-cache tests: 10/10 passed.
- The dependent record/index stack, which contains this exact base, passed 267 total tests: 262 passed, 5 hardware skips, 0 failed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- No package/dependency changes.

This PR is based directly on `v1.8.6` (`383bc029`).

title: Improve legacy WPF visualization responsiveness
body:
## Summary

This extracts the baseline-compatible legacy WPF/OxyPlot responsiveness work from #398, following the review request.

It deliberately avoids statistics algorithms, timing-source behavior, record parsing, persistence, and build tooling so the 1.x UI work can be reviewed independently.

## Plot rendering

- Decimate dense OxyPlot lines in screen space while preserving raw source points.
- Preserve first/last points, per-column minima/maxima, ordering, and non-finite gaps.
- Keep tracker, zoom, and export behavior on full-resolution data.
- Batch plot invalidation so each refresh is rendered once.
- Represent constant average/threshold lines with two endpoints instead of one point per frame.

## WPF and selection responsiveness

- Keep recycling virtualization on the main record grid.
- Keep row/column virtualization on the aggregation grid, but use Standard mode because its outlier background is assigned directly to row containers; Recycling could retain stale colors after scrolling.
- Load selected captures outside the UI thread.
- Serialize loads, cancel obsolete requests, and prevent stale publication.
- Reuse the selected session for double-click navigation and observe/log background faults.
- Debounce rapid comparison-slider redraws.
- Derive comparison bounds from already-rendered finite series points instead of analyzing sessions twice.

## Deliberately excluded

- Statistics correctness/performance and timing-source changes.
- Record parsing, caching, and persistent indexing.
- DataViewModel/threshold/synchronization work requiring new statistics APIs.
- Aggregation session/array retention.
- Build tooling and dependencies.

## Validation

- x64 Release application build: passed, 0 errors.
- x64 Release test build: passed, 0 errors.
- Focused UI/rendering tests: 7/7 passed.
- Full suite: 261 total, 256 passed, 5 hardware-dependent skips, 0 failed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- No package/dependency changes.

The five commits remain separated into rendering, virtualization, selection loading, comparison redraw, and the reviewed aggregation-highlight fix.

This PR is based directly on `v1.8.6` (`383bc029`).

title: Fix timing statistics correctness and source consistency
body:
## Summary

This extracts the statistics-correctness work from #398 into a focused change, following the review request.

It fixes invalid timing handling, outlier boundaries, variance classification, timing-source consistency, and related depiction/export behavior without including the separate statistics-performance work.

## Statistics correctness

- Reject non-finite, zero, and negative frametime/display samples before analysis.
- Preserve valid zero values for GPU/CPU active timing while rejecting negative/non-finite values.
- Apply outlier removal after time-window selection and preserve the original timestamps of surviving points.
- Remove exactly the slowest 0.1% for deci-percentile filtering, including the exact 1,000-sample boundary.
- Preserve constant sequences and handle duplicate cutoff values by count.
- Return the unchanged sequence for unsupported outlier modes instead of `null`.
- Make variance bins mutually exclusive, ignore non-finite adjacent pairs, and return finite zeroes when no pairs exist.
- Preserve multi-run boundaries so comparison variance never introduces an artificial pair between captures.

## Timing-source consistency and depiction

- Use display-change timing only when every compared session/run supports valid present and display timing; otherwise all records use present timing.
- Keep Average FPS present-based.
- Apply the resolved source consistently to low metrics, line/FPS/distribution/L-shape/variance charts, sorting, and labels.
- Add an explicit timing-source label in the comparison UI.
- Filter report and online timing metrics consistently and fall back to present timing when display samples are unavailable.
- Align GPU-active clipboard export by timestamp intersection and exclude non-finite pairs.
- Use separate scratch storage/locks for realtime and five-second online calculations and cleanup.

## Deliberately excluded

- Batch metric APIs and sorted-sequence caching.
- Sparse distribution performance.
- Record parsing/loading and persistence.
- WPF background loading, virtualization, and OxyPlot decimation.
- Build tooling and dependency changes.

## Regression coverage

Tests cover invalid timing, active-time zeroes, timestamp-preserving outliers, exact percentile boundaries, constant/duplicate sequences, unsupported modes, variance bins, multi-run boundaries, display distribution source, comparison source fallback, and aligned clipboard data.

## Validation

- x64 Release application build: passed, 0 errors.
- x64 Release test build: passed, 0 errors.
- Focused frametime-statistics tests: 37/37 passed after the final review fixes.
- Full suite: 270 total, 265 passed, 5 hardware-dependent skips, 0 failed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- No package/dependency changes.

This PR is based directly on `v1.8.6` (`383bc029`). The clean statistics-performance delta is staged at fpsheaven/CapFrameX#1 and will be submitted upstream after this foundation lands.

title: Upgrade GitHub Actions to latest versions
body:
### ci: update GitHub Actions to silence Node.js runtime deprecation warnings

#### Summary
This PR updates the github-actions in `main.yml` to their latest supported versions.

The current workflow triggers runtime deprecation warnings on `windows-latest` runners:
> `Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24...`

Upgrading these action versions eliminates these warnings and ensures long-term pipeline stability before GitHub completely drops Node 20 execution support on runners.

---

#### Changes
- Updated `actions/checkout`, `setup-dotnet`, `upload-artifact`, `download-artifact`, `setup-msbuild`, and `setup-nuget` to their latest releases.

Beyond updating the actions, this change addresses security vulnerabilities present in older versions. It also provides a minor performance boost for upload-artifact and download-artifact.

Of course, there's no need to rush this, as version bumps can sometimes introduce unexpected bugs. However, in this case, these newer versions have been tested and haven't shown any issues so far.

As a potential qof improvement down the road, it might also be worth enabling Dependabot on a monthly schedule, purely to keep us informed about available updates.

---

#### Verification
Tested on a fork build: binary builds, installers, and artifact uploads executed with 0 errors.
https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/32256357077

title: fix(IGCL): resolve compiler warnings in IGCLManager
body: I noticed that in each GitHub Actions run, there are about 40 warnings (according to the last one). Yes, the vast majority are normal warnings and nothing to worry about, but I found some that are highly fixable, especially in `IGCLManager.h` and `IGCLManager.cpp`. - Fix inconsistent DLL linkage: IGCLManager.h declared all exported functions as __declspec(dllimport), while IGCLManager.cpp defines them in this same project (CapFrameX.IGCL.dll). Changed to __declspec(dllexport) to match. Resolves 6x C4273 warnings (IntializeIgcl, CloseIgcl, GetAdpaterCount, GetBusWidth, GetDeviceInfo, GetIgclTelemetryData). - Remove unnecessary `typedef` on IgclTelemetryData and IgclDeviceInfo. C++ struct declarations already name the type; no alias was ever used. Resolves 2x "typedef ignored" warnings. - Fix signed/unsigned comparison in GetBusWidth: igcl_api.h defines ctl_mem_properties_t::busWidth as int32_t, where -1 means "unknown". Comparing it directly against the local uint32_t accumulator implicitly promoted -1 to UINT32_MAX, letting an "unknown" reading win the max-width comparison. Now guards against non-positive values before the unsigned comparison. No behavioral change is expected from the linkage/typedef cleanup. The busWidth fix corrects a latent edge case that only triggers when a memory module reports an unknown bus width. --- Verification: builds cleanly, and these 9/10 warnings no longer appear in the build output. https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/32315430590 I also ran the app from that specific run and nothing seems to be broken, so I would like to get your thoughts on this. Thanks!

title: Fix SHA1Managed obsolete warning (SYSLIB0021) in StringExtensions
body:
`GetSha1` used `SHA1Managed`, which is obsolete since .NET 5 (SYSLIB0021). Replaced with `SHA1.HashData()`, the modern static helper, and simplified the hex-encoding loop to `Convert.ToHexString()`.

No behavioral change: output format and hashed bytes are identical to the previous implementation.

---

Verification:
https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/32357470966

title: fix(Hwinfo): use conditional export/import macro for HWINFO_API
body: Same issue as the recent `CapFrameX.IGCL` fix (#412): `TimeStampCounterFrequency.h` declared `GetTimeStampCounterFrequency` as `__declspec(dllimport)`, but it's defined within this same project (`CapFrameX.Hwinfo.dll`), causing an "inconsistent dll linkage" warning. Switched HWINFO_API to the same conditional export/import macro pattern already used by ADLX_API and (now) IGCL_API, keyed off `CAPFRAMEXHWINFO_EXPORTS`, which the project already defines in all four build configurations, so no .vcxproj changes were needed. Verified: builds cleanly, warning no longer appears in the build output. https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/32437049892

title: Remove dead vendored OxyPlot source and empty CapFrameX.Constants project
body:
Deletes `source/CapFrameX.Charts/OxyPlot/` and `source/CapFrameX.Charts/OxyPlot.Wpf/` - a full vendored copy of the OxyPlot library (373 files, ~3.4MB), including a `OxyPlot_SL5.csproj` targeting Silverlight 5.
Deletes `source/CapFrameX.Constants/` - a project with zero `.cs` files, only a `netstandard2.0` `TargetFramework` and an `OxyPlot.Core` `PackageReference`.

**Why**

Neither `OxyPlot.csproj`, `OxyPlot.Wpf.csproj`, nor `CapFrameX.Constants.csproj` is listed in `CapFrameX.sln`, and no other `.csproj` in the solution has a `ProjectReference` to any of them.  App already consumes OxyPlot through the `OxyPlot.Core` **NuGet package** in `CapFrameX.ViewModel`, `CapFrameX.Data`, `CapFrameX.View`, `CapFrameX.Test`, `CapFrameX.PMD`, and `CapFrameX.Statistics.PlotBuilder`, so the vendored source tree is a stale duplicate, not a live dependency. `CapFrameX.Constants` has no code and isn't imported anywhere (`grep -r "using CapFrameX.Constants"` returns nothing).

**How this was verified**

- Cross-referenced every `.csproj`/`.vcxproj` on disk under `source/` against `CapFrameX.sln` - these three were the only solution-relevant projects present on disk but absent from the `.sln`. (`CapFrameX.VoltageMonitor` is also absent from the `.sln` but is a working, up-to-date standalone diagnostic app, not dead/duplicate code - intentionally **not** touched here).
- Confirmed no CapFrameX-specific code anywhere references OxyPlot's chart types that lived in the vendored copy (`OldCandleStickSeries.cs` etc.) - further sign this was inherited demo content from upstream OxyPlot, never wired into the app.

Build/runtime verification (done locally on Windows after applying the patch):
- Full solution build completed with no new errors or warnings introduced by this change.
https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/32538630800
https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/32539366946
- App launched normally afterward. No behavioral or visual differences observed anywhere charts are rendered (Comparison tab, run history, overlay chart mode), consistent with the vendored copy never having been part of the compiled output to begin with, since it was already outside `CapFrameX.sln` before this PR.

---

 **Charting**
 - `CapFrameX.Charts/Core40` - Core charting engine
-- `CapFrameX.Charts/OxyPlot` - OxyPlot library
 - `CapFrameX.Charts/WpfView` - WPF chart controls
+- OxyPlot is consumed via the `OxyPlot.Core` NuGet package, not from source - do not reintroduce a vendored copy under `CapFrameX.Charts/`

Mouse placement uses the real cursor position, which is always + correct regardless of the rotation. title: Prism 9.0.537 upgrade
body:
### Summary

**1. Versions Update (9 .csproj files)**
* Updated `Prism.Core`, `Prism.Wpf`, and `Prism.DryIoc` to version `9.0.537` across all projects.
* This includes `CapFrameX.PMD`, which was successfully upgraded from `7.0.0.396` to match the rest of the solution.

**2. DryIoc Dependency Bump (5 .csproj files)**
* Upgraded `DryIoc.dll` from `4.1.0` to `5.4.3` in the following projects: `CapFrameX.Extensions`, `CapFrameX.Test`, `CapFrameX.Remote`, `CapFrameX`, and `CapFrameX.Mcp`.
* This satisfies the minimum requirement for `Prism.Container.DryIoc` (`>= 9.0.106`) and removes the version mismatch between what this app referenced and what `Prism.DryIoc` was compiled against.

**3. Namespace Refactoring**
* Migrated `Prism.Regions` to `Prism.Navigation.Regions` across 14 files (13 ViewModels + `Bootstrapper.cs`), plus the fully-qualified reference in `RegionManagerWrapper.cs`.

**4. Bootstrapper.cs**
* `IContainerProvider.GetContainer()` no longer exists in Prism 9 - replaced with a direct cast to `DryIocContainerExtension` and its `.Instance` property (`Prism.Container.DryIoc` namespace), which is what that extension method did internally.
* Removed the custom `CreateContainerRules()` override. It existed to work around a historical binary mismatch between Prism 7.2.0.1422 (compiled against DryIoc 4.0.7) and this app's DryIoc.dll pin (4.1.0). With DryIoc.dll now aligned to 5.4.3, that mismatch no longer exists, and Prism 9's own internal default rules are more complete.

**5. Xaml Behaviors Alignment (3 .csproj files)**
* `Prism.Wpf` `9.0.537` requires `Microsoft.Xaml.Behaviors.Wpf >= 1.1.122`. The repo had it pinned to `1.1.39` in `CapFrameX.View`, `CapFrameX.ViewModel`, and `CapFrameX.MVVM`. All three have been updated to `1.1.122`.

**6. UseInstance Removal**
* `IContainer.UseInstance()` no longer exists in DryIoc 5.x (it was split into `RegisterInstance`/`Use` a while back, and the old alias was finally dropped). Replaced both call sites - the `ILoggerFactory` registration in `CapFrameX.Extensions/ContainerExtensions.cs` and the `IShell` registration in `Bootstrapper.cs`- with `RegisterInstance`, matching the pattern already used everywhere else in this codebase.

**7. XML Namespace Migration in Shell.xaml**
* `Shell.xaml` was still using the legacy XML namespace identifier (`http://www.codeplex.com/prism`, from the Prism 4/5 era) instead of the one every other view in the solution uses (`http://prismlibrary.com/`). Prism 9 dropped backward-compatibility mapping for the legacy URI during its Regions cleanup. Migrated it to match the rest of the codebase.

---

**Potential improvements from this upgrade:**
- Removes historical workarounds required to bridge Prism 7 with newer DryIoc versions.
- DryIoc 5.x brings performance and allocation improvements over the 4.x line this app was previously locked to (not independently benchmarked in this PR).
- Keeps XAML/WPF dependencies on actively maintained versions.

---

**I recommend not merging this PR just yet.** I am still performing QA testing on this major change. So far, it doesn't seem to have broken anything "at the moment," but I am still testing it thoroughly.

**Manual QA checklist (in progress):**
- [x] Region navigation across all tabs (Comparison, Cloud, Colorbar, PMD, Info, Data, Aggregation, Overlay, Sensor, Report, Capture)
- [x] Clean shutdown after a capture session — no lingering process/handles

Your verification, feedback, and potential improvements or anything I might have missed would be highly valuable @DevTechProfile

Feel free to test it out if you'd like: (verification)
https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/32796450443

title: Log missing first-run config files as Debug instead of Error
body:
### Summary

On a clean portable install, `CapFrameX.log` shows `Error`-level entries for `SensorEntryConfiguration.json` and `Processes.json` on first launch:

Error while loading sensor config. Default config loading instead...
System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not find file '...\Config\SensorEntryConfiguration.json'.
...
Error while reading from file.
System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not find file '...\Config\Processes.json'.

Neither is an actual error, both are the expected "first run, config file doesn't exist yet" case, and both already fall back correctly (`SensorConfig` to its default dictionary, `ProcessList` to the bundled `ProcessList/Processes.json` template). The exception is just being used as control flow instead of being checked for up front.

Compare with the line right above them in the same log, for `AppSettings.json`, which already does this correctly:

File '...\Config\AppSettings.json' does not exist. Creating it...

### Changes

**`CapFrameX.Sensor/SensorConfig.cs`**
* `GetInitializedSensorEntryDictionary()` now checks `File.Exists()` before reading. If the file isn't there yet, logs at `Debug` and returns `null`, letting the existing fallback in `LoadOrSetDefault()` load defaults exactly as before. A file that exists but fails to read/parse (corrupt JSON, permissions) still throws and still logs as `Error`, unchanged.

**`CapFrameX.Data/ProcessList.cs`**
* `Create()` now checks `File.Exists()` before calling `ReadFromFile()`. If it's not there yet, logs at `Debug` and falls through to the existing bundled-defaults logic further down (unchanged). Genuine read failures still log as `Error`.

### Testing
Verified on a portable session on a fresh folder, both entries now log at `Debug` instead of `Error`, with identical fallback behavior (defaults load the same way, capture starts normally). Full log attached below for reference:

https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/33014546613

`{"@t":"2026-08-26T21:23:20.3794677Z","@mt":"Sensor config file not found at {Path}; using defaults.","@l":"Debug","Path":"C:\\Users\\test\\Downloads\\9aab0781b4d10103c7b74afa916b6336ace78911_portable\\Portable\\Config\\SensorEntryConfiguration.json"}`

Bump a few low-risk packages, drop dead dependencies

**Version bumps (all patch/minor, no breaking API changes):**

- EmbedIO 3.4.3 → 3.5.2 (CapFrameX.Remote, CapFrameX.Mcp, CapFrameX)

Bumping EmbedIO raised its floor on Unosquare.Swan.Lite to >=3.1.0, which

6.0.0 pin in CapFrameX.View. Bumped that one too.

- `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design` (Webservice.Host), no DbContext anywhere in the repo, leftover from before the EF persistence layer was dropped
- `Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design` (Webservice.Host), scaffolding tool, not referenced anywhere

title: Implement CPM for NuGet
body:
Moves all NuGet package versions from individual .csproj files to a single `Directory.Packages.props` file. This change standardizes dependency versions across all projects in the `source/` directory, simplifying future package updates and reducing potential version conflicts.

if we ever need to pin a specific version for whatever reason, we can still do that with the correct typo, that's why I added comments to both new files.

```xml
<PackageReference Include="example-package" VersionOverride="1.2.3" />
```
That keeps the shared default intact for everyone else and makes the exception
visible in the project that needs it.

What changed:
- Added `source/Directory.Build.props`, turns on
  `ManagePackageVersionsCentrally`. Scoped to `source/` (not the repo root) on
  purpose: `pmcreader-plugin/` and `capframex-linux/` are separate project
  trees outside CapFrameX.sln and must not inherit this.
- Added `source/Directory.Packages.props`, one `<PackageVersion>` per
  distinct package (79 total) used anywhere under `source/`.
- Every `PackageReference` in the 32 affected `.csproj` files dropped its
  `Version=` attribute; the version now comes from the central file.

Verified: https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/33234429991

title: Suggestion: bump to .NET 10
body:
.NET 9 is an STS release, and its support window ends this coming November 2026 (matching .NET 8's end of support). .NET 10 is an LTS release supported until November 2028, so upgrading to .NET 10 now buys us over two years of stability instead of having to re-do this migration again in just a few months.

Also `Directory.Packages.props` already has a bunch of `Microsoft.Extensions.*` / `System.*` packages pinned to `10.x` versions, so the TFM was arguably already lagging behind what we're actually shipping.

### What changed (branch https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/tree/net10)

Bumped every project under `source/` that was on `net9.0-windows`/`net9.0` to `net10.0-windows`/`net10.0` (24 + 4 projects), plus `CapFrameX.RTSSInterface.vcxproj` which also carries a managed `TargetFramework` (C++/CLI, `CLRSupport=NetCore`).

Left untouched on purpose:
- `capframex-linux`, separate Avalonia port, `net8.0`, unrelated
- `CapFrameX.Webservice.Host` / `.Implementation`, still `netcoreapp3.1`, that's its own migration
- `CapFrameX.CustomInstallerActions`, `.NET Framework 4.7.2`, pinned by WiX v3
- all the `netstandard2.0` libs, intentionally portable
- `pmcreader-plugin`, still on `net9.0-windows`, lives outside `/source`, punted for now

Other stuff that had to move with it or CI would've broken:
- `CapFrameX.OSD.Integration.csproj` resolved the prebuilt `CapFrameX.OSD.Interop.dll` HintPath via `$(TargetFramework)`, but `external/CapFrameX.OSD-prebuilt/` only has a `net9.0-windows/` folder, pinned that HintPath to the literal folder name instead of chasing the TFM.
- `CapFrameXInstaller.wixproj` (BinaryDir + the heat.exe pre-build), `Build-And-Run.ps1`, all had `net9.0-windows` hardcoded as the output path.

### Status

Already ran a full pipeline on this and it's green: SDK setup picks up 10.0.400, `CapFrameX.csproj` build (which drags in the RTSSInterface native/CLI project) succeeds, installer and bootstrapper builds both succeed too. So the risky part - the C++/CLI project actually working under the new CLR - is confirmed fine.

https://github.com/independent-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/33461915758

If you agree, I could open the PR, I suppose there are still a few things that need to be moved to .NET 10, like pmcreader for example, which will still remain on .NET 9.
But at least, we won't have to worry about this for a long time again, and I think it's a positive thing to align ourselves with this LTS.

title: Stale "Important Message" banner shows on every fresh install
body: Just did a clean portable install (currently on 1.9.1.1 beta) and got greeted with the orange "Important Message" banner about missing sensor data on 1.7.6 or lower / the 2025 1.7.7 beta. Never ran anything close to that version, so the message is meaningless here. Dug into it a bit - it's not baked into the release, `ColorbarViewModel.GetAppNotification()` pulls it live from the webservice on every launch: if (notification.IsActive && notification.Timestamp > _appConfiguration.LastAppNotificationTimestamp) So the client only checks "have I already dismissed this exact message" (via the saved timestamp in config), never "does this even apply to my version." On a fresh install `LastAppNotificationTimestamp` is empty, so whatever's currently flagged active in the CMS shows up unconditionally. That message has been sitting there since the 1.7.x migration and nobody's flipped `IsActive` off since. Suggestion: 1. Short term, someone with Squidex access just needs to turn that one off (or update it to something actually current). 2. Longer term this'll keep happening for whatever the next announcement is, since there's no way for the client to know a message has aged out. Adding a min/max app version to `SqAppNotificationDataDTO` and checking it client-side alongside the timestamp would let old messages expire on their own instead of relying on someone remembering to deactivate them by hand.

title: Hook-free renderer: frametime chart stalls repeatedly, stall duration scales with PresentMon replay buffer
body:
## Summary

With the built-in hook-free renderer, the overlay's frametime/FPS chart advances,
then freezes, then jumps ahead to catch up, repeating continuously. The stall duration
tracks the `PresentMon replay buffer` setting: at the default 2500 ms the chart freezes
for roughly 2.5 s at a time, and lowering the value shortens the stalls accordingly.
Lowering it does not remove them. The buffer appears to be drained and refilled before
playback resumes, instead of being played out continuously to smooth the stream.

## Environment

- CapFrameX 1.9.0 (internal 1.9.0.8, release channel), installer package
- PresentMon 2.5.1 (bundled)
- PawnIO 2.2.0.0 (official signed edition)
- .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (x64)

## Relevant settings (OSD options)

- Overlay renderer: CapFrameX hook-free
- Hook-free output display: unset (dropdown still shows the "Display" placeholder)
- Chart refresh rate: 10 Hz
- PresentMon replay buffer: 2500 ms
- Overlay refresh period: 1000 ms
- Real-time metrics interval: 5 s
- Smooth numeric values: on
- Background opacity: 85 %, Overlay size: 100 %, Anchor: Bottom left (X 5 / Y 1155)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Select the CapFrameX hook-free renderer.
2. Start a game and enable the overlay with a frametime chart entry.
3. Watch the chart: it advances, stalls, then jumps ahead.
4. Change the PresentMon replay buffer value and repeat: the stall duration changes
   with it.

## Expected

Chart advances continuously; the replay buffer smooths burstiness in the PresentMon
stream at the cost of a constant added latency.

## Actual

Chart advances, stalls, then catches up in a jump, repeating. Stall duration is a
function of the replay buffer value.

## What I already tried

I adjusted the renderer-related settings individually, including the replay buffer,
the chart refresh rate and the overlay refresh period. Changing the buffer only scales
how long each stall lasts; it does not make the chart run continuously. None of the
other settings changed the behavior.

## Notes

- Extended OSD logging was off during the observation. Happy to enable it and attach
  per-present logs, or record a short clip of the overlay, if that helps.

title: Hook-free overlay anchors to the desktop work area, not the monitor bounds (taskbar on top or side offsets the overlay)
body:
## Summary

With the hook-free renderer, overlay placement seems to be relative to the desktop
work area rather than the physical monitor bounds. With the Windows taskbar positioned
at the top left of the screen, an anchor with X 0 / Y 0 does not put the overlay in the
screen corner; it lands below the taskbar, offset by the taskbar height. The effective
placement range is shifted for every anchor, and there is no way to reach the area the
taskbar occupies. The only workaround i found is to anchor it to the bottom and use 
really high Y values, but this causes shifting on overlay edits.

## Environment

- CapFrameX 1.9.1 Beta installer package
- Overlay renderer: CapFrameX hook-free
- Windows taskbar position: top

## Steps to reproduce

1. Move the Windows taskbar to the top of the screen (might require Windows Insider builds).
2. Select the CapFrameX hook-free renderer.
3. Set an anchor (e.g. top left) with X 0 and Y 0.
4. Enable the overlay.

## Expected

X 0 / Y 0 places the overlay flush in the chosen corner of the monitor.

## Actual

The overlay is offset by the taskbar height, sitting below the taskbar instead of in
the corner. The same shift applies to all offsets, so the reachable placement area is
reduced by the taskbar.

## Suggested fix / feature request

Either of these would solve it, in order of preference:

1. Anchor overlay placement to the monitor bounds rather than the work area, so offsets
   are measured from the physical screen edges regardless of taskbar position. This
   makes coordinates predictable and independent of the user's shell layout.
2. If work-area-relative placement is intentional, allow negative X and Y offsets so
   the overlay can be moved into the taskbar area manually.
3. Optionally, a toggle between "monitor bounds" and "work area" as the placement
   reference, for users who explicitly want the overlay to avoid the taskbar.

title: Request: Digitally Sign CapFrameX in-game/hook-free Overlay Renderer Libraries
body:
Hello. This is more of a inquery/request than an issue report.

Currently, most CapFrameX in-game/hook-free overlay renderer libraries (dll/bin files) are flagged/blocked by Smart Access Control (SAC) on Windows 11 because MS doesn't know the author or flag it as untrusted. The consequence is that CX may fail to load these newly built-in CX overlay components (RTSS renderer components are not affected) during CX launch, while triggering Windows Security SAC notifications and even blocking the program launch.

The workaround is easy: Disable Smart Access Control (SAC) via the Windows Security dashboard. I tried adding CX folders to Windows Security/Defender exclusions, but SAC still flags/blocks the CX built-in overlay renderer components regardless of such custom folder exclusions.

My question and request:

Are there any plans to digitally sign the CX overlay renderer libraries? This would allow users to keep SAC enabled while using the latest versions of CX (1.9+) without encountering Windows Security SAC warnings or program component blocks. If you haven't considered this yet, could you please look into it?

Best regards

title: Add a localization layer, with Russian as the first catalog
body:
## Summary

Adds a small localization layer so the interface and the overlay can be translated without changing saved data. English remains the default and the source language of every string. Russian is the first catalog, included to prove the path and to give one complete translation.

A new language is another embedded catalog plus an entry in the language list. It does not need new markup.

The fork-only portable prerelease workflow is not part of this pull request.

## Settings

- Settings → Application has two independent choices: interface language and overlay language.
- Both are stored on the existing configuration (`UiLanguage`, `OverlayLanguage`) and applied at startup.
- Allowed values are `en` and `ru`. English is the fallback when a key is missing.

## Translation mechanism

- `CxLang` loads one embedded JSON catalog. The catalog has three sections:
  - `ui`: exact strings for the application
  - `overlay`: exact names for overlay rows and status text
  - `phrases`: ordered replacements for sensor names and units that are built at runtime
- `{loc:Tr 'English source'}` marks a visible string. On a real element it follows the current interface language. Inside a template, where the target does not exist yet, it returns the translated text. Returning a `Binding` from that path was tried and rejected: WPF stored the binding in the template and the page failed to load.
- Enum `[Description]` and `[ShortDescription]` go through the same catalog.
- Sentences built in code (capture status, update status, the record search bar, the sensor evaluation button) are translated where they are produced.
- Record-list columns are found by `x:Name`, not by the visible header. After the headers were translated, a lookup for `"Game"` / `"CPU"` / `"RAM"` threw in `ControlView.SetHeaders()` and left every tab blank.

## Overlay

- Profiles, sensor identifiers, and capture files stay in English.
- The overlay list shows a translated description and group name. RTSS format tags such as `<S2><C1>` stay out of the grid.
- Units and hardware words are replaced only as whole words or complete phrases, so `VRAM Used` is not partly rewritten as `RAM Used`.
- A label that occupies its own line is capitalized. Replacements used in the middle of a name stay lowercase.
- Capture-service and hook-status text is translated. Product names, driver versions, and other reported hardware strings are not.
- The overlay page width is unchanged, and graphs are still only drawn for frametime, framerate, and display time.

## Russian catalog

- Covers the main windows, settings, dialogs, status bar, capture, aggregation, comparison, sensors, PMD, cloud, report, synchronization, and the chart-control help (`HelpTexts/ChartControls.ru.rtf`).
- Includes overlay sensor phrases (units, CPU, GPU, memory, and drive names).
- A few labels are shorter than a literal translation so they fit the existing controls.

## Not changed

- Process names, URLs, product names, and the abbreviation FPS.
- Overlay profile JSON keys and capture file contents.
- Which overlay rows can show a graph.
