title: Migrate the installer to WiX Toolset v6.0.2
body:
Both installer projects are now SDK-style WixToolset.Sdk 6.0.2 projects restored from NuGet, so the build machine no longer needs a WiX installation.

- Product.wxs / Bundle.wxs: v4 schema (wix convert), plus the manual steps: platform-suffixed util custom actions, formatted bundle variables, bal:Condition attributes, ExePackagePayload.
- The heat.exe pre-build step and filter.xslt are replaced by a <Files> element with the same exclusions; CapFrameX.dll.config is added back explicitly. The generated CapFrameX.Binaries.wxs is gone.
- The bundle stays 32-bit (InstallerPlatform=x86) like the v3 bundles.
- VC++ redist remote payloads are verified by their signing certificate; v4+ rejects a hash next to certificate attributes.
- theme.xml ported to the v4 thmutil schema, based on the v6 RtfLargeTheme, keeping the CapFrameX layout.
- Custom actions move to WixToolset.Dtf 6.0.2.
- CI drops the wix314.exe install and builds the .wixproj with /restore.

WiX v4+ derives an ExePackage's cache id from the payload hash. The VC++ redistributables are verified by their signing certificate instead, so the build failed with WIX0010 until each package names its own CacheId.

Refs Fixes CXWorld#420

---

This moves the installer and the bootstrapper to WiX Toolset v6.0.2.

## Changes

**Projects**
- `CapFrameXInstaller.wixproj` and `CapFrameXBootstrapper.wixproj` are SDK-style projects (`<Project Sdk="WixToolset.Sdk/6.0.2">`). MSBuild restores WiX from NuGet, so nothing has to be installed on the build machine.
- `WixToolset.Util.wixext` and `WixToolset.Bal.wixext` 6.0.2 are added to `source/Directory.Packages.props`.
- The unused `WixUIExtension` and `WixNetFxExtension` references are dropped.
- `CapFrameX.CustomInstallerActions` moves from `WixToolset.Dtf.*` 5.0.2 to 6.0.2.

**MSI (`Product.wxs`)**
- Converted to the v4+ schema with `wix convert`, plus the steps the converter leaves for manual work:
  - `WixCloseApplications` becomes `override Wix4CloseApplications_X64`.
  - `WixCA` becomes `Wix4UtilCA_X64`.
  - `Win64` becomes `Bitness`.
  - Standard directories are declared with `StandardDirectory`.
- The `heat.exe` pre-build step and `filter.xslt` are replaced by a `<Files>` element with the same exclusions, as `<Exclude>` entries.
- `CapFrameX.dll.config` is added explicitly, since `*.dll.config` is excluded.
- The generated `CapFrameX.Binaries.wxs` is removed.
- `InstallerPlatform` is pinned to x64.

**Bundle (`Bundle.wxs`, `theme.xml`)**
- The bundle stays 32-bit (`InstallerPlatform=x86`), like WiX v3 bundles.
- `BootstrapperApplicationRef` becomes `BootstrapperApplication` with `Theme="rtfLargeLicense"`.
- Bundle variables use `Type="formatted"`, the v4+ equivalent of v3's `string`.
- `bal:Condition` uses the `Condition` attribute.
- `DisplayInternalUI="no"` is removed.
- VC++ redistributables:
  - `RemotePayload` becomes `ExePackagePayload`.
  - WiX v4+ rejects a hash next to the certificate attributes, so the payloads are verified by `CertificatePublicKey`/`CertificateThumbprint` and the SHA-1 hashes are removed.
  - Each package gets an explicit `CacheId`, which WiX requires in that case.
- `theme.xml` is ported to the v4 thmutil schema, based on the WiX v6 `RtfLargeTheme.xml`. It keeps the CapFrameX layout: 500x555 window, banner, version on the banner, colours and the configuration-import text.
- The v3 `FilesInUse` page is dropped because it is no longer a WixStdBA page.

**CI (`main.yml`)**
- The `wix314.exe` install step is removed.
- The `.wixproj` builds run with `/restore`.

**Docs**
- `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `dev-plans/MCP_Integration_DevPlan.md` are updated.

## Verification

- CI builds the app, the MSI and the bootstrapper: https://github.com/indep-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/36019209486
- Tested:
  - [x] Clean install: installed files match the previous version (`CapFrameX.dll.config`, `vulkan\`, `hook\`, `PresentMon\`), shortcuts are created, and the Vulkan layer is registered in both registry views.
  - [x] Upgrade over 1.9.1 replaces the old version, with no duplicate entry in Programs and Features.
  - [x] Bootstrapper UI renders correctly: banner, version, text, Options page.
  - [ ] On a machine without the VC++ redistributables, the bootstrapper downloads them and accepts their signature.
  - [x] The in-app updater installs with `LAUNCHAPP=1` and CapFrameX starts afterwards.
  - [x] Repair and uninstall work, and the prompt to close CapFrameX still appears.

title: Run the installer's uninstall cleanup only on a real uninstall
body:
Follow-up to the review in #446. These issues predate the WiX migration.

## Changes (`Product.wxs`)
- `CleanRegistry` and `AppdataConfigFiles` run only on a real uninstall (`REMOVE="ALL" AND NOT UPGRADINGPRODUCTCODE`). Before, a repair or modify deleted the autostart task and the `*.json` files in `%appdata%\CapFrameX`, and `CleanRegistry` also ran on every install and upgrade.
- `CleanRegistry` is now `Execute="deferred" Impersonate="no"`, like `PurgeVulkanLayers`, so removing the Task Scheduler task and the HKLM `Run` value runs in the elevated service context. `RemoveAutoStartKey` reads no session properties, so no code change is needed.
- `AppdataConfigFiles` stays immediate: it has to run as the user to reach the user's `%appdata%`.
- The Vulkan cleanup actions are unchanged; they still run on install, repair and upgrade.

Upgrades from 1.9.1 and earlier still run the old conditions once, because the old MSI is removed with its own sequence.

## Verification
- [x] Repair keeps the `CapFrameX` scheduled task and the `*.json` files in `%appdata%\CapFrameX`.
- [x] Uninstall removes both.
- [ ] Upgrading to a later build keeps both.
- [x] A bundle repair succeeds on a machine with a newer VC++ 2015-2022 runtime installed.

title: Update dependencies, modernize project files and fix installer location and downgrades
body:
## Summary

Two commits:

1. **Update packages, modernize project files and replace obsolete APIs**
2. **Install the x64 app into Program Files instead of Program Files (x86)**

https://github.com/indep-arg/CapFrameX/actions/runs/37670620254

### 1. Dependencies, project files, obsolete APIs

**Packages** (`source/Directory.Packages.props`)
- MSTest 3.6.1 → 4.4.1 (every 3.x is deprecated as *Legacy* on NuGet), Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.10.1, Moq 4.20.72.
  Tests migrated from the removed `[ExpectedException]` / `Assert.ThrowsException` to `Assert.ThrowsExactly`, and from the obsolete `[DataTestMethod]` to `[TestMethod]`.
- Serilog 2.9 → 4.4 (Sinks.File 7, Formatting.Compact 3, Extensions.Logging 10, Sinks.Console 6.1, Serilog.AspNetCore 10).
- .NET 10 servicing: `Microsoft.Extensions.*` and `System.*` aligned on 10.0.12; Jwt 8.23, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4, HidSharp 2.6.4, SerialPortStream 2.4.2, TaskScheduler 2.12.2.
- Removed 11 PackageReferences that the .NET 10 shared framework already provides (NU1510) and the PackageVersion entries nothing references.
- Removed `ConsoleAppLauncher` (referenced but never used) and its `NU1701` suppression.
- MouseKeyHook 5.6 → 5.7.1 (ships `net6.0-windows` assets); now referenced only by `CapFrameX.Hotkey`.

**Webservice host:** `Program.cs` moves from the obsolete `WebHost` to the generic host (Serilog.AspNetCore 10 only supports `IHostBuilder`); `KnownNetworks` → `KnownIPNetworks`.

**CapFrameX.CustomInstallerActions:** SDK-style `net472` project with central package versions; `packages.config` and `..\..\packages` HintPaths are gone. The `.CA.dll` still bundles `Microsoft.Win32.TaskScheduler.dll`, `WixToolset.Dtf.WindowsInstaller.dll` and `CustomAction.config`; TaskScheduler satellite resource assemblies are excluded because MakeSfxCA packs files flat. The .NET Framework 4.7.2 targeting pack is no longer needed to build it.

**Project files:** removed properties that restate SDK defaults (`Deterministic`, `AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath`, `RootNamespace`/`AssemblyName` equal to the project name, `LangVersion latest`, default `OutputPath` blocks), an empty `ProjectExtensions` block, and `GeneratePackageOnBuild` in the embedded LibreHardwareMonitorLib (it produced an unused `.nupkg` on every build plus NU5100 warnings).

**Obsolete APIs**
- `LoginManager`: `WebRequest` → `HttpClient` (same request body and content type, still throws on non-success status codes; the userinfo request no longer blocks a thread), `RNGCryptoServiceProvider` → `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes`, `SHA256Managed` → `SHA256.HashData`.
- `RecordManager`: `SHA1Managed` → `SHA1.Create()` (same hash).

**Bug fix:** `JsonSettingsStorage` passed an argument without a placeholder to `LogError` (CA2017), so the information was lost. It now logs the path and the entry count, and no longer interpolates the path into message templates.

### 2. Install folder

The bootstrapper is a 32-bit Burn bundle, so `[ProgramFilesFolder]` resolves to `Program Files (x86)`. Its `InstallFolder` variable is forwarded to the MSI as `INSTALLFOLDER` and overrode the MSI's `ProgramFiles64Folder` default, so the **64-bit app was installed into `C:\Program Files (x86)\CapFrameX`**. The bundle now uses `[ProgramFiles6432Folder]`.

Upgrading an existing installation moves it: the major upgrade removes the files and registry values from the x86 folder, and the shortcuts, `InstallDir` and the Vulkan layer registrations are recreated from `INSTALLFOLDER`. The autostart task needs no migration because the app re-registers it with its current path on every start (`ColorbarViewModel.OnAutostartChanged(true)`).

## Verification

### Done
- [x] CI green on both commits: app, native DLLs, installer and bootstrapper. In the installer step, `MakeSfxCA.exe` produced `CapFrameX.CustomInstallerActions.CA.dll` with TaskScheduler and DTF next to it.
- [x] CI warnings: NU1510, NU1701, NU5100, SYSLIB0014/0021/0023 and CA2017 are gone; the remaining ones were already there.
- [x] Evaluated MSBuild properties (OutputPath, OutDir, PlatformTarget, AssemblyName, RootNamespace, TargetPath, …) are identical before and after the project-file cleanup for 37 projects × Release|x64, Debug|x64, Release|x86; the only difference is `LangVersion` `latest` → `14.0`, the same language version on .NET 10.
- [x] Hook-free Vulkan overlay on vkcube reaches `Vulkan verdict: Success` with the layer registered from `C:\Program Files\CapFrameX`.
- [x] App, tests and webservice compile with 0 errors; the webservice host builds with 0 warnings.

**Installer (manual, Windows 11)**
- [x] Fresh install lands in `C:\Program Files\CapFrameX` (was `Program Files (x86)`).
- [x] Upgrade over an install in `Program Files (x86)`: app moved to `Program Files`, old folder removed, settings in `%appdata%` kept; desktop, taskbar and start-menu shortcuts work.
- [x] Uninstall: the migrated custom actions remove the scheduled task, the install folder and the Vulkan layer registrations in both registry views; nothing in HKCU.
- [x] Reinstall works.

**App (manual)**
- [x] `CapFrameX.log` written in compact JSON with structured properties (Serilog 4); no errors.
- [x] Global hotkeys (MouseKeyHook 5.7.1): capture hotkey (0 ms latency) and ALT+O overlay toggle.
- [x] Capture of vkcube: 1201 frames at 60 FPS, CPU/GPU/RAM sensor data recorded, valid SHA-1 run hash; opens in Analysis.
- [x] A capture recorded with an older version still loads and analyses correctly.
- [x] Settings persist across restarts.
- [x] Autostart: the task is registered with `C:\Program Files\CapFrameX\CapFrameX.exe` and starts the app at logon; disabling it removes the task.
- [x] PresentMon starts and the update catalog check succeeds.

### Pending
- [ ] Unit tests locally (MSTest 4): `vstest.console source\CapFrameX.Test\bin\x64\Release\net10.0-windows\CapFrameX.Test.dll /Platform:x64`; the workflow does not run tests.
- [x] Cloud login / token refresh / upload (`HttpClient` in `LoginManager`), if the cloud feature is still used.
- [ ] PMD / Benchlab over USB/serial, if the hardware is available.
- [x] Webservice host starts with the generic host, routes requests through MediatR, returns 401 on protected endpoints and logs requests through Serilog.AspNetCore 10 (local run with placeholder settings; Squidex calls need the production credentials).

## Not in this PR
- MaterialDesign 5.3, System.Reactive 7, DynamicData 9, OxyPlot 2.2, NAudio 3, gong-wpf-dragdrop 4: major/UI-visible updates that need UI testing.
- Webservice: MediatR / FluentValidation.AspNetCore are also *Legacy* on NuGet; MediatR 13+ and AutoMapper 15+ are commercially licensed.
- `OxyPlot Axis.AxisChanged` stays: obsolete, but OxyPlot offers no replacement event.
- Pre-existing warnings: unused fields in `ThreadAffinityController` (the feature is disabled: `_isSupportedCPU` is never set), `catch (Exception ex)` in `RecordManager`, C4267 in the RTSS wrapper, LibreHardwareMonitorLib.

title: [Bug] CapFrameX 1.9.2.1 incorrectly reports P1 (1% Low) at approximately 59.6 FPS
body:
### Description

CapFrameX 1.9.2.1 appears to incorrectly calculate or display the P1 (1% Low) metric.

When opening previously recorded benchmark data, P1 is reported as approximately **59.6 FPS** across multiple recordings, regardless of the actual frame-time distribution.

The same recordings show correct P1 values in **CapFrameX 1.9.1**, matching the results calculated independently from the raw JSON data using a custom analysis tool.

This suggests a regression in the P1 calculation or display logic introduced in version 1.9.2.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open CapFrameX 1.9.2.1.
2. Load an existing benchmark recording that displays the correct P1 value in CapFrameX 1.9.1.
3. Check the P1 (1% Low) metric in the analysis results.
4. Observe that P1 is reported as approximately 59.6 FPS.
5. Open the same recording in CapFrameX 1.9.1 and compare the results.

### Expected Behavior

P1 should be calculated consistently from the recorded frame-time data and should match the result produced by CapFrameX 1.9.1 when analyzing the same recording.

### Actual Behavior

P1 is reported as approximately 59.6 FPS for multiple recordings, including older benchmark results that previously displayed correct values.

### Environment

- CapFrameX affected version: 1.9.2.1
- CapFrameX comparison version: 1.9.1
- OS: Windows 11 Home, Build 26200
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
- GPU driver: 610.88
- Example game: Marvel Rivals (DirectX 12, 2560×1440)

### Additional Information

The raw JSON recording contains frame-time data that produces substantially different P1 values from the approximately 59.6 FPS shown in version 1.9.2.1.

The issue also affects recordings captured before updating to 1.9.2.1, suggesting that the original capture data is not necessarily corrupted.

I can provide a sample JSON recording for reproduction.

title: Comparison: Frame Time Distribution chart stays empty after switching the theme
body:
### Description
After switching between light and dark mode, the Comparison → Frame Time Distribution chart loses its series: only the grid and the refresh-rate lines are drawn, and the axes fall back to their defaults. The data comes back only after switching to another chart tab and back.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Comparison: add two or more records and open **Frame Time Distribution**.
2. Open the settings and toggle **Dark mode** (either direction).
3. Close the settings: the distribution chart is empty.
4. Switch to **Variances** and back: the chart is drawn again.

### Expected
The chart is redrawn with the new theme colors and the same data.

### Actual

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1a8686c-32a5-4ba4-a021-2e3e0a7b0d80

### Cause
`ComparisonViewModel.SubscribeToThemeChanged()` calls `InitializePlotModels()`, which replaces the frametime, FPS and distribution plot models with new, empty ones, and then `UpdateChartsSafely()`. `UpdateCharts()` only fills a model whose `_is…ChartDirty` flag is set, and the theme handler does not set them, so a chart that was already drawn stays empty until something else marks it dirty.

### Suggested fix
Mark the charts dirty before redrawing:

    _eventAggregator.GetEvent<PubSubEvent<ViewMessages.ThemeChanged>>()
        .Subscribe(msg =>
        {
            InitializePlotModels();
            SetChartUpdateFlags();
            UpdateChartsSafely();
        });

### Notes

- The Analysis tab: its theme handler rebuilds the whole page
  (`UpdateAnalysisPage()`). It can show a brief flash while it rebuilds, then renders correctly.
- Environment: CapFrameX 1.9.2.1 beta (portable)

title: Remove .NET Framework configuration leftovers
body:
.NET 10 ignores `bindingRedirect`, `<startup>` and `legacyCorruptedStateExceptionsPolicy`, and `ConfigurationManager` only reads the executable's config (`CapFrameX.dll.config`), so the libraries' `app.config` files are never read. Checked with a small .NET 10 app: a redirect to a nonexistent version was ignored, and a library's own `.dll.config` was never loaded.

- Remove the 21 library `app.config` files. They only held binding redirects; the one in `CapFrameX.Configuration` also had 82 `userSettings` for a `Properties.Settings` class that no longer exists. The installer already excluded their `*.dll.config` copies.
- Remove the empty `Settings.settings`/`Settings.Designer.cs` and `Resources.resx`/`Resources.Designer.cs` templates of `CapFrameX` and `LiveCharts.Wpf` (no settings, no resources, no references) and the unused `WpfView.nuspec`.
- `App.config` keeps only the `appSettings` the app reads. `ClientSettingsProvider.ServiceUri` was not read by anything.

The build output now has a single `CapFrameX.dll.config` with the 9 keys; the installer is unchanged.

title: Allow turning the overlay renderers off completely: the in-game hook is injected even with the overlay disabled
body:
## Summary

With the default renderer (**CapFrameX in-game**), turning the overlay off (the "Overlay active" switch / ALT+O) only hides it. CapFrameX still injects the hook into every DXGI game it detects. There is no setting that keeps CapFrameX from injecting into games or creating a renderer while you still use it for captures.

## Current behaviour

The two config flags `EnableHookOverlay` / `EnableHookFreeOverlay` encode the three renderer choices (`OverlayViewModel.SetOverlayMode`). `IsOverlayActive` is a separate visibility switch:

| Renderer | With `IsOverlayActive = false` |
|---|---|
| CapFrameX in-game (default) | `HookOverlayManager` keeps the process-start watcher and the early-injection probe armed, and calls `TryInjectAsync` for the selected PID as soon as PresentMon reports a DXGI runtime (`OnFrameRow`: `if (_enabled) TryInjectAsync(pid)`). Injection depends only on `_enabled` (`EnableHookOverlay`), the target policy and the compatibility gates, not on `IsOverlayActive`. The hook stays resident and only skips drawing (`HookVisibilityChannel`). The status bar shows `Hook: Waiting` meanwhile. |
| CapFrameX hook-free | Nothing is injected, but `OsdOverlayBridge` keeps the native renderer alive and cloaked while the mode is selected. This is deliberate, to avoid the DWM stalls of tearing it down. |
| RTSS | No CapFrameX renderer and no injection. The radio button is disabled unless RTSS is installed. If neither flag is set and RTSS is missing, `OverlayService` sets `EnableHookOverlay = true` at startup ("RTSS is not installed. Selecting the CapFrameX in-game overlay as the default renderer."). |

So on a system without RTSS, the lightest possible state is the hook-free renderer with a hidden window. Editing `AppSettings.json` to clear both flags doesn't help, because startup switches back to the in-game renderer.

## Why it matters

- **Captures only:** many people use CapFrameX only for frame time captures. They expect "overlay off" to mean that nothing is loaded into the game.
- **Problem isolation:** when a game misbehaves (crash, anti-cheat, another overlay), turning the overlay off is the obvious thing to try. Today it doesn't remove the hook, so it can't rule it out.
- **#460 fits this pattern:** Hogwarts Legacy crashes on launch with 1.9.2.x "even with the overlay disabled", using default settings, so the in-game renderer is selected. It is not confirmed that the hook is the cause (no logs yet), but disabling the overlay could not have prevented an injection there. An "Off" option would give that user a clear workaround and a clean A/B test.

## Proposal

Add a fourth choice, **Off**, to *Overlay renderer*:

- no hook injection: no process-start watcher, no early-injection probe, no `TryInjectAsync`;
- no hook-free host;
- no RTSS feed;
- captures, sensors and the remote API (`/api/osd`, `/ws/osd`) keep working;
- the overlay hotkey has no effect (or shows a short hint);
- it can be selected whether or not RTSS is installed, and the startup normalization in `OverlayService` leaves it alone.

Two booleans can't hold a fourth state cleanly, since both false already means "RTSS". A small enum setting (`Rtss`, `InGame`, `HookFree`, `Off`), migrated once from the two flags, would keep the gating in `OverlayService` / `HookOverlayManager` / `OsdOverlayBridge` simple.

**Alternative considered:** don't inject while `IsOverlayActive` is false, and inject when it is turned on. I'd rather not do this as the only fix. Turning the overlay on mid-game would then always mean a late injection, which breaks the titles that need early injection (`d3d12.dll` / `sl.interposer.dll` gate, frame generation). ALT+O would also stop being an instant show/hide. An explicit "Off" keeps today's behaviour for people who use the overlay.

## Minor, related

With the overlay switched off, the status bar still reads `Overlay: Off` together with `Hook: Waiting`, which suggests something is still pending. Once "Off" exists, the hook status could read `Off` / `Disabled` instead.

title: Clean up leftover files and fix the VoltageMonitor build
body:
This is a follow-up to #465 that picks up the optional suggestions from that review, plus a couple of things I found along the way. It's split into three commits, so any of them can be dropped on its own.

**1. Leftovers from the old LiveCharts package**

When LiveCharts was copied into the repo, some files from its NuGet packaging came along that nothing uses anymore:

- `install.ps1`: all it did was open the LiveCharts website after a package install.
- `docs.xml` and `wpf.docs`: old generated documentation. Nothing builds or reads them, and they still mention the resources we removed in #465.
- Five ReSharper settings files (`*.csproj.DotSettings`). They only forced the C# 5 language level, and four of them are named after projects that no longer exist.

I also updated the comment in `Product.wxs` next to the `*.dll.config` exclusion, since the libraries no longer have their own config files. The exclusion stays as a safety net.

**2. The old `nuget.exe`**

You suggested removing `nuget.exe`, but `scripts/Build-And-Run.ps1` still used it, so I looked into that first. It turns out to be NuGet 3.4.3 from 2016, which is too old to understand how this repo manages packages today, so its restore step wasn't doing anything. The `dotnet restore` right after it is what actually restores the packages. I removed that step and the 3.9 MB executable.

**3. VoltageMonitor didn't compile**

The Panther Lake voltage monitor isn't part of the solution, so it never gets built with the rest, and that's how this slipped through. During the localization work its window texts were switched to translation keys, but the tool has no access to the app's localization, so it fails to compile. Since it's a small standalone diagnostics tool, I gave it back its English texts and removed the five keys from the language files, because nothing else uses them. The localization test still passes. If you'd rather keep it translatable, it would need a reference to `CapFrameX.MVVM` instead.

The app, the tests and VoltageMonitor all build without errors, and the warning count is unchanged.

title: Fix/axis title margin
body: The frame time axis title got cut off when a recording has very large spikes (e.g. 20000 ms during a loading screen). Analysis (`PlotBuilder`) and Comparison used a fixed left plot margin (50 and 40 px). Five-digit tick labels don't fit in that space, so OxyPlot pushed the axis title out of the chart. This isn't related to the OxyPlot update: 2.1.0 and 2.2.0 render it identically. The left margin is now automatic, so it grows with the labels; the other sides keep their fixed values, so the right side stays reserved for the percentage axes. PMD, Synchronization and Capture are unchanged. In a regular recording the automatic margin ends up a few pixels narrower than the old 50 px. A new rendering test, `FrametimeGraph_LargeFrametimes_KeepTheAxisTitleInPlace`, checks that a recording with a 22000 ms spike keeps the axis title where a regular recording has it. With the old fixed margin it fails (the title moves from x=21 to x=5).

title: End PresentMon when CapFrameX is closed or crashes
body:
## What happened

If CapFrameX got closed from Task Manager, crashed, or hung while closing, PresentMon kept running in the background. It kept capturing and, since it runs from the app folder, it kept that folder locked. With the portable version you couldn't delete the folder until you found `CX-PresentMon-2.6.1-x64.exe` in Task Manager and ended it by hand. I ran into this several times without noticing what it was.

## The fix

When PresentMon starts, it now goes into a kill-on-close job object, using the same `ChildProcessJob` the Benchlab process already uses. Windows closes that job when CapFrameX exits, no matter how it exits, and takes PresentMon down with it. The normal shutdown hasn't changed: it still stops PresentMon through `--terminate_existing_session` first.

If the job can't be created for some reason, it's only logged as a warning and PresentMon starts as before.

## Tests

- New integration test `PresentMon_EndsWhenCapFrameXReleasesItsJob`: it starts the real PresentMon, releases the job the way Windows does when CapFrameX exits, and checks that PresentMon ends.
- Manual (portable build): ended `CapFrameX.exe` from Task Manager, first from the Processes tab and then from the Details tab (hard kill, nothing logged on exit). PresentMon went away with it both times, the portable folder could be deleted, and the next start brought up PresentMon normally.

title: Only redraw Comparison charts when a range value is entered
body:
## What happened

In Comparison, every key press in the range **Start** / **End** boxes redrew all charts. That includes arrow keys, Shift and holding Backspace. The boxes only take the new value when they lose focus, so each of those redraws used the old range anyway. With 10 records of 100k frames, each redraw takes about 100-200 ms on the UI thread, so typing "120.5" meant five full redraws for nothing.

## Fix

The charts are redrawn on **Enter** only, the same way the Analysis page already handles its range boxes.

## Tests

Manual: typing in Start/End no longer redraws anything; pressing Enter applies the range.

title: Zero-pad the time in capture file names
body:
## What happened

Capture files were named with the hour, minute and second written without leading zeros, e.g. `...-2026-10-15T10174.json` for 10:17:04. That makes different times of the same day give the same name: 1:11:11, 11:01:11 and 11:11:01 all become `T11111`. Records are saved with `FileMode.Create`, so the later capture silently overwrote the earlier one. Cloud downloads were named the same way.

## Fix

Both now use `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HHmmss` with the invariant culture, e.g. `T101704`. The invariant culture also stops a culture with another calendar (Thai, for example) from changing the year. Nothing in the code parses these names, and existing files keep their names.

## Tests

- `GetCaptureFilename_PadsTheTimeOfDay`
- `GetCaptureFilename_DifferentTimesOfADay_GiveDifferentNames`
- `FormatFileTimestamp_IgnoresTheCurrentCulture`

title: Escape the cloud upload description
body:
## What happened

The description you type for a cloud upload was put into the request URL as is. An `&` or `#` in it cut the description off at that point, and a `+` arrived as a space.

## Fix

The description is escaped with `Uri.EscapeDataString`. The webservice reads it with `[FromQuery]`, which decodes it back.

## Tests

- `GetUploadRequestUri_EscapesTheDescription`
- `GetUploadRequestUri_DescriptionRoundTrips`
- `GetUploadRequestUri_NoDescription_SendsAnEmptyParameter`

title: Make "Cut record" fast on long sensor logs
body:
## What happened

"Cut record" froze the UI on records with long sensor logs. A 5 h log at 250 ms (72,000 samples) took about **150 s**. Two parts were quadratic:

1. Each kept sensor sample was copied with `Values.ElementAt(index)`. `Values` is a `LinkedList`, so every call walked the list from the start.
2. `NormalizeStartTimesOfSessionRuns` read `BetweenMeasureTimes` twice per sample, and that property copies the whole list into a new array on every read. This also runs when an aggregated record with more than one run is saved.

While fixing the first one I also found an off-by-one in the guard before the copy. A sensor with exactly as many values as the index of the last kept sample made `ElementAt` throw, and the whole cut was dropped with only a log line.

## Fix

- The sensor values are copied to an array once and indexed.
- The intervals are read once.
- A sensor that is too short is now left empty, as one with fewer values already was, and the cut is written.

With both fixes, the 5 h log is cut in about **1 s**.

## Tests

`RecordManagerCutTest`:

- inside and inverse cuts keep the right sensor samples;
- a short sensor no longer drops the cut;
- a 72,000-sample log is cut within 10 s.

title: Find portable records in the MCP tools
Fix raw sensor copy and cut thread
body:
## Copy raw sensor info was O(n²)

"Copy raw sensor info" on the Analysis page built each row by reading every exported sensor property again. Each read rebuilds an array from the sensor's linked list. The GPU-limit share, which walks the whole GPU load, was also recomputed for every row. On the UI thread that took about 1.5 s for 4,000 measure times, and several minutes for a 5 h log at 250 ms.

The table is now built by `RawSensorInfoExport`, which reads each column and the GPU-limit share once per run. The copied text is unchanged. A 5 h log now takes about 0.1 s.

## Cut record ran on the UI thread

`DuplicateSession` only awaits after it has cloned, filtered and normalized the whole record, so the window froze until the cut was written. The command now runs it with `Task.Run`, using the session and range from the moment of the click. A click while a cut is running is ignored, just as the blocked window ignored it before. `DuplicateSession` needs nothing from the UI thread and catches its own errors.

## Tests

- `RawSensorInfoExportTest`:
  - the output is identical to a verbatim copy of the previous implementation;
  - header and row count;
  - a 5 h log finishes within 30 s.
- Cut in the background: manual. The window stays responsive and the cut record appears in the list.

title: Feature request: Configurable text outline/stroke for the built-in overlay
body:
### Feature request

Please add an optional configurable outline/stroke around the text rendered by CapFrameX's built-in overlay.

### Reason

I am using CapFrameX 1.9.2.1-beta without RTSS. The new built-in overlay font looks clean and modern, but the text can become difficult to read over bright or visually busy game scenes because it lacks a contrasting outline.

To clarify, I am not referring to a background panel or a drop shadow. I mean a thin outline that follows the outer edge of each character, similar to the text rendering commonly seen with RTSS.

### Suggested options

- Enable/disable text outline
- Configurable outline color, with black as the default
- Configurable thickness, such as 1–2 px
- Ideally available for both the in-game and hook-free renderers

I think even a subtle 1 px black outline would greatly improve readability while preserving the clean appearance of the new font.

title: Tolerate non-finite sensor samples in SessionSensorData2
body: LibreHardwareMonitor occasionally records a NaN sample for every sensor during one polling cycle (glitched hardware read). The SessionSensorData2 getters used Convert.ToInt32 over raw doubles, which throws OverflowException on NaN/Infinity and aborts DataViewModel.UpdateAnalysisPage midway: PC latency is assigned before the throw, everything after (charts, sensor table) silently never updates. Replace direct conversions with a safe converter (NaN/Inf -> 0, out-of-range clamped) and filter non-finite samples before the GPU limit-time aggregation in SensorReport.

title: Import sensor data embedded in FrameView CSV logs (fixes #267)
body:
Fixes #267 — FrameView log CSVs carry sampled hardware sensor columns (board power,
clocks, utilization, temperatures, CPU power, battery), but the import only took the
framerate/PCL columns, so the diagrams had no power values.

**Merge target:** `release/1.9.3` (1.9.2 is feature-frozen). Single commit, based directly on
`release/1.9.3`. FrameView writes `"NA"` for unsupported metrics; those cells stay NaN, align
with the measure-time axis and pass through `FillMissingValues` like any other sample.

What this does:

- New `FrameViewSensorColumnMapper` maps the sensor columns of FrameView log files
  (1.2 through 2.x) onto CapFrameX session sensor entries with LibreHardwareMonitor-style
  naming ("GPU Core", "CPU Total", ...), so they show up in the same charts and sensor
  report as native captures.
- Power values requested in #267: `NvPwr(W)(API)` (GPU board power), `GPUOnlyPwr`,
  `AMD Pwr`, PCAT power total, `CPU Package Power(W)`; GPU/CPU clocks, utilization and
  temperatures plus battery metrics are mapped as well.
- `CPUClk` maps to "CPU Average" (Clock): the FrameView user guide (1.2/1.4) documents
  it as the *average* CPU frequency, not the per-core maximum.
- Intel hybrid CPUs: per-cluster `E-Core Power(W)` / `P-Core Power(W)` are merged into a
  "CPU Package (E+P Cores)" power entry when the package power column is all-NA (common on
  these platforms). The name is deliberately kept distinct from a real package power reading
  (a core-cluster sum is not package power), while still feeding
  `SessionSensorData2.CpuPower`. A real package power column that reported values always
  wins over the merge.
- Header matching normalizes case/whitespace, so layout changes between FrameView
  versions ("GPU0Clk(MHz)" vs "GPU0Clk (MHz)") keep working.

Robustness:

- CSVs without embedded sensor data (PresentMon, MangoHud, ...) match zero columns and
  take the exact same code path as before.
- Unrecognized columns are ignored; columns that never report a value are skipped.
- `"NA"` cells stay NaN and align with the measure-time axis.

Tests: `FrameViewSensorColumnMapperTest` covers 1.2 vs 1.4+ header layouts, the 1.7
cluster-power and battery columns, degree-sign variants, PresentMon-style headers
(no match), duplicate headers (first occurrence wins) and null input.

title: [Bug] Main window exceeds available screen width at 200% Windows DPI scaling
body: ## Description CapFrameX 1.9.2 does not fit properly on a 2560 × 1600 display using Windows 11's recommended 200% scaling. The main dashboard extends beyond the visible window boundaries, clipping the GPU information panel and other content on the right. The application also cannot be freely resized or snapped using Windows 11's Win + Arrow shortcuts. ## Environment - **Application:** CapFrameX 1.9.2.4 - **Distribution:** Portable ZIP (Scoop extras bucket, version 1.9.2) - **OS:** Windows 11 IoT Enterprise, Build 26200 - **Device:** Lenovo Legion 5 Gen 10 (AKP10) - **Display resolution:** 2560 × 1600 (native) - **Windows scaling:** 200% (Recommended) - **Effective desktop resolution:** 1280 × 800 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Set Windows display resolution to 2560 × 1600. 2. Set Windows display scaling to 200%. 3. Launch CapFrameX 1.9.2 Portable. 4. Observe the Info dashboard. 5. Attempt to resize the application window or use Windows Snap shortcuts. ## Actual behavior - Dashboard content extends beyond the visible window boundaries. - Information panels on the right are partially clipped. - The application cannot be resized sufficiently to fit the available desktop. - Windows Snap shortcuts do not provide usable tiled layouts. ## Expected behavior - The application should remain fully usable at Windows-recommended DPI scaling. - Dashboard panels should adapt to the available window width, wrap, or support horizontal scrolling where appropriate. - The application should support smaller window sizes where technically feasible. ## Additional context The CapFrameX 1.9.1 release notes mention a minimum/default window size of **1488 × 768**. At 200% scaling, a 2560 × 1600 display provides approximately 1280 × 800 device-independent pixels, which appears insufficient for the current minimum window width. Reducing system-wide DPI scaling should not be necessary simply to use the application. ## Additional testing: 150% vs 200% scaling I tested CapFrameX 1.9.2 at both 150% and 200% Windows display scaling, keeping the native resolution at 2560 × 1600. **Results:** - **200% (Windows recommended):** The application exceeds the available desktop width, resulting in clipped navigation elements and dashboard panels. - **150%:** The entire application becomes visible and the dashboard renders correctly. This strongly suggests that the minimum window width (1488 logical pixels) exceeds the available workspace at 200% scaling (1280 logical pixels). While reducing the scaling to 150% resolves the clipping, it makes the rest of the Windows desktop and other applications uncomfortably small. ## Requested improvement Please consider a responsive layout for smaller logical desktop resolutions, including: - Adaptive dashboard panel arrangement. - Scrollable content where necessary. - A reduced minimum window width. - Improved compatibility with Windows Snap layouts. Ideally, CapFrameX should remain usable at the display scaling recommended by Windows without requiring system-wide scaling changes. ## Screenshots ### Windows Display settings (200%) ### CapFrameX at 200% scaling (clipped UI) ### CapFrameX at 150% scaling (working UI)

title: Add Simplified Chinese (zh-CN) localization
body: ## Add Simplified Chinese (zh-CN) localization This PR adds a Simplified Chinese UI catalog, following the "Adding a new language" steps in the README. It targets `release/1.9.3` and includes the new profile-merge strings. ### Files - `source/CapFrameX.Contracts/Localization/zh.json` – full catalog: all 1636 `strings`, all 96 `overlay` labels, and 198 `phrases` rules for OSD sensor names (same patterns as `ko.json`, Chinese replacements). - `source/CapFrameX/HelpTexts/ChartControls.zh.rtf` – translated chart controls help. - `README.md` – lists Simplified Chinese (`zh`) under available languages. - `external/CapFrameX.OSD-prebuilt/Localization/Editor.zh.json` and `Templates.zh.json` – Chinese catalogs for the tile overlay designer (525 + 148 keys, same keys and placeholders as the 1.9.3 en files). The designer catalogs are embedded in `CapFrameX.OSD.Controls.dll` from the private OSD repository, so these two files can't take effect from this repo. Please copy them into the OSD repo's catalogs if you'd like the designer translated too. ### Translation conventions - Technical terms are shown bilingually where space allows, e.g. `帧时间 (Frametime)` and `1% Low 平均值 (1% low average)`. Short labels, `_Short` keys and OSD labels use Chinese only, or keep the English abbreviation (FPS, P1, 1% Low, GPU-Busy, …). - Product names, abbreviations, units and present-mode names stay in English. ### Checks - `CxLang.ValidateCatalog` accepts `zh.json`, and every `phrases` pattern compiles as a .NET `Regex`. - Key sets match `en.json` for `strings` and `overlay`. The `{n}` placeholders and `\n` counts match for every key. - Tested in a 1.9.2.4 installation with a rebuilt `CapFrameX.Contracts.dll` that embeds `zh.json`. The interface and OSD language can both be switched to 简体中文 in Settings. Screenshots below. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Feature Request: Hotkey to freeze overlay metrics like (AVG FPS, 1% Low) after a benchmark run is completed
body:
### **Feature request** 

Please add a toggle option to lock the final overlay metrics (AVG FPS, 1% Low) on screen after a benchmark run is completed, so the values don't update until a new capture is started or un-frozen manually.

### **Reason**

I am using CapframeX 1.9.2.4 without RTSS (Tile Overlay). This feature would be very useful for users coming from MSI Afterburner, where that feature already exists and you can check benchmark results without leaving the game.

### **Other Suggestions**

- Configurable frametime graph size for RTSS Overlay

- Fixing a Bug, that makes it impossible to change colour of the "API" settings in the Overlay Editor, it stays gray.

Thanks for the great software and work in this project

title: Microsoft Defender flags v1.9.2 installer ZIP as Trojan:Win32/Cloxer
body:
Microsoft Defender on Windows 11 flags the official **v1.9.2 installer archive** as `Trojan:Win32/Cloxer`.

**Download:**
https://github.com/CXWorld/CapFrameX/releases/download/v1.9.2/release_1.9.2_installer.zip

An existing download was detected on November 23, 2026. I then tried downloading it again twice using Chrome, and Defender blocked both attempts before I ran the installer.

Windows Security reports:
- **Severity:** Severe
- **Category:** Trojan
- **Status:** Removed
- **Affected file:** `release_1.9.2_installer.zip`

The exact detection name was confirmed in Defender's operational log.

#### Steps to reproduce
1. Download the installer archive from the official release link using Chrome.
2. Defender flags and removes the download.

#### Defender versions
At the initial detection:
- **Security intelligence:** `1.463.439.0`
- **Engine:** `1.1.26100.4`

#### Screenshot
![Windows Security flags the CapFrameX v1.9.2 installer archive as a severe Trojan threat and reports it removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0a81221-f9ae-4e9b-8ec2-94bce4c46206)
